properties.body:
## The default path (short; machinery engages only on signals)

1. **Understand as a habit** — the Method runs internally (ask,
   audience, artifacts, person, organization, composition — including
   the standing UNIT question: which axes — structural / temporal /
   spatial — what hierarchy; "none" and "sequence-of" are legal;
   "cannot tell" escalates). Surface to the owner ONLY what is
   genuinely ambiguous, batched into one question sheet, conversation
   available on any line of it.
2. **Work** — one agent per unit of work, with a brief that is a
   constraint-set + provisioned data + model tier (never a persona);
   iterate against the deterministic judge where one exists.
3. **Floor + present** — the honest floor: remaining disagreements
   named and classified (gap / taste / error). Present the COMPLETED
   artifact with the floor census and margin attached — never
   fragments, never diffs.
4. **Iterate / consent** — harvest owner comments (deduce
   defect/taste/question; never demand a format; convert theirs if
   they use one); answer questions first; taste persists as steering.
   Consent is asked when canon mutates or work publishes — not as a
   completion ritual.

Engagement signals that bring machinery in: no deterministic judge →
critique ensemble (weight inversely proportional to judge strength);
mute single-shot generator → composition ensemble ahead of the shot;
units > 1 → shard by unit + a cross-unit coherence expert; repeated
worker/judge disagreement → second opinion; stuck → escalate with work
shown. When a gate engages, review BRIEF CONTENT, not cast topology.
Plan generation is one seeded casting step, never a meta-ensemble.

## The flow

### 1. Recon (read-only; no human) — sealed reading FIRST
**The reading is sealed before the mapping opens** (owner-ruled): read
and comprehend the artifact ON ITS OWN TERMS — structure, vocabulary,
fact-grain claims, its own internal contradictions — BEFORE any canon
query. A reader whose head is full of canon assimilates the artifact
to existing categories before it has finished speaking, harmonizes
contradictions it should surface, and misses genuine deviations; the
kernel (metaontology structure) may inform the reading, project canon
may not. Only when comprehension is complete does the mapping open:
each artifact-local claim judged against canon — same-as / extends /
new / contradicts — every mapping a recorded Opinion with confidence,
low confidence batching to the owner's question sheet. (Held as
discipline — the lens system that will enforce it physically is
designed and built (the engine's lens module and its lenses design
record — `python -m graph docs lenses`); the seal
becomes physical when the declarations take graph residence at the
owner's gate.)

Open the reading room first: `python -m graph comprehend <artifact>`
fingerprints the source and builds its structure (section tree, bodies,
order, embedded-table refs) in the comprehension workspace, filing the
flat archive under `graph/comprehension/`. A non-text artifact (an
image, a PDF, audio) is not read for structure: it enters at its
**floor receipt** — `python -m graph receipt <file>` prints its
fingerprint, size, and the medium its bytes declare — cited by
fingerprint on the citizen it is about, with an observation of what
it shows; the room refuses it plainly, receipt in hand. At the diff
gate a citizen named for a file under the knowledge base must carry
that file's fingerprint. An artifact is a citizen of its own: an
`[Artifact]` named for a stable handle, WHERE it is on
`[Artifact Location]` rows behind LOCATED_AT (`[File Location]` for a
path under the knowledge base — the gate reads it, records
verification on the row, derives fingerprint and medium; any other
kind rests unverified by design), its grade two facets
— what the source says (the documentary chain, decaying as links
rot) and what was examined (Cited until a description and its
DEPICTS facts are confirmed at a gate, then Attested). Comprehending the
description yields the DEPICTS candidates — the objective contents,
one edge per thing, a song depicting a horn as surely as a picture,
each pairing asked its role at the door (is this the thing's
reference — primary — or does the artifact also-show it?); a primary
pairing's reference interpretation derives by itself in the same
round, so never author the boilerplate — and a candidate with no
citizen in canon is a gate question with two answers: CREATE HERE
(an ordinary citizen of this world; the edge lands) or IGNORE,
RECORDED (an `[Approved Omission]` of that fact, so re-scans never
re-ask; the description keeps the word) — never a dangling edge or a
free-text tag. What the artifact STANDS FOR is an `[Interpretation]`:
one per intent, ABOUT the artifact, INTERPRETED_AS its subject,
DRAWS_ON the depicted things it uses. Canon is the subject matter,
never the document — the artifact's insides live here, not as canon
citizens; artifact quirks
(duplicate headings, odd nesting) are absorbed silently, never surfaced
to the submitter. Then read the source cold. Identify — by **semantic
comprehension, never word search** — every entity, relationship, and
rule it asserts, whatever the casing discipline. Resolve pronouns and indirect references; ambiguity
that survives multiple passes becomes an owner question, never a guess.
Resolve every candidate through the graph (read-only Cypher + the term
index; `python -m graph terms` is the mechanical backstop, not the
method). Check the stub worklist (`MATCH (s:Archetype {stub: true})`) and
prior Judgment rows — the term may already be a known-open item. Bucket
findings: *relates-to* / *introduces* / *uncertain*, with grades.
**A machinery risk you can verify during recon is a recon task, not a
risk to carry into the round**: read the code or run the tool now, and
if the gap is real, its ask joins the owner's collated sheet as a
numbered question. A "named risk" in the plan that a five-minute read
would have settled resurfaces later as a mid-round interjection — the
costlier shape.

### 2. The plan gate (the approver)
Present the what's-this-about proposal, **leading with the implications
preview**: what the approver GETS, what they LOSE or change, what it
AFFORDS later — each with a concrete example from the corpus. Then the
interview, per ontology-intake's discipline (three tiers; scenario
questions; the owner names everything and rules everything —
explicitly, never by silence). The interview arrives as ONE collated
question sheet — every question batched with its cited evidence,
named tension, consequences, and a recommendation; serial pinging is
not a permitted shape (see that skill's interview step).
Procedure-shaped content inside the source
follows procedure-intake at this point. Nothing has been written
anywhere.

### 3. Schema is ground on the graph — and changes by ceremony
The schema stratum (the concept citizens and their edges) is ground
truth on the graph itself: post-bootstrap machinery reads it from the
graph, never from a schema file, and the schema anchor's version
auto-stamps from the event-log sequence at apply. **Schema changes
ride the schema ceremony**: an owner-gated round may add a new
DECLARED concept (the Archetype arrives WITH its DECLARED_IN edge, and
usually INSTANCE_OF into its parent), birth a new LABEL (a
spec-carrying row arriving WITH its DECLARED_IN edge, permitted only
when the base holds no ground rows under it — nothing yet underneath,
so nothing moves), edit a schema row's doc text,
add an ALIAS to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an
existing citizen — additions only, each target existing in the base or
born by the same round),
edit a label's RENDER MAPPING (the table layout it renders through —
add, change, or remove; the loader never reads it, so nothing moves),
release a program label's FILES (the registered file list leaves the
spec once every citizen carries its own program body and cites no
file — from then on a body is a ground prop, edited in a round like
any other, re-lifted at apply),
declare a TAXONOMY link (an authored kind-of connection into a concept,
both citizens existing in the base or born by the same round), or
remove an UNREFERENCED schema row — the delta report itemizes these
under its marked ceremony section, and the owner's approval of that
round IS the ceremony ruling. A round may also DECLARE MOVES in
`graph/proposals/current/moves.json` — a RENAME of the world's own
label or concept (old name -> new name: the schema row and everything
under it, every citizen relabeled, every connection re-pointed, every
spec binding and the attribution ledger rewritten) a RE-HOMING of
named citizens under a kind of what they were (a SUBTYPE_OF-descendant
label, so no fact is lost and derivation keeps them instances of the
source), and a CITIZEN RENAME (label -> {old name -> new name}: the
citizen's identity whole — every property travels, every connection
re-points, the attribution ledger follows — what a by-hand
remove-and-add loses; names resolve through the round's label
renames, and a rehomed citizen's name resolves through its own
rename). The gate itemizes each move with its counts and refuses by
name a new name already held, a kernel name (a kernel rename is a
kernel ceremony), a re-home target that is not a kind of the source,
or a citizen not under the source; the proposal embeds the moves so
the approval covers them; apply performs them after the authored
changeset (spoken in the old names, as scratch was cut — a taxonomy
declaration for a renamed concept is authored under the old name and
re-pointed) and records the inverse as the full ground diff. Everything
else on the stratum — other spec/catalog changes, referenced
removals — still
refuses by name (data moves underneath those; they ride the migration
charter) and PARKS as a Question at the plan gate for the owner to
rule and sequence; it never blocks the fact-plane work that doesn't
need it, and it is never worked around with a lesser encoding. Facts
whose schema doesn't exist yet wait with their Question.

The from-sources era is closed: the graph is the only schema
surface, and no bootstrap file mirrors anything.

### 4. Scratch authoring (agent + machine)
Reset scratch first (`python -m graph restore --database scratch`, using
the KB's own working-copy name if its settings declare one) — stale
scratch produces phantom diffs, and the round machinery refuses a copy
whose in-band identity does not match the round. **The standing first authoring move is
clearing the previous round's debts**: stamp that round's shipped PR
link onto its Judgment rows, and land any edges it deferred under
marker rows whose endpoints now exist in canon. A round that skips the
opening move leaves the debt to compound — one round of lag is the
design; two is a backlog. Then author **ground facts** through the
`neo4j-scratch` MCP connection, the way agents naturally work: create,
query your own work, fix, iterate.
- MATCH existing endpoints, MERGE only the new node/relationship (a
  whole-path MERGE duplicates existing nodes and trips the uniqueness
  constraint).
- Every non-obvious fact carries its receipt as properties: `from_text`
  (a verbatim SENTENCE-GRAIN source quote — never a table row: a cell's
  facts land as structured properties, and the delta gate refuses a
  row-shaped receipt), `source` (where), `grade: 'agent-proposed'`.
  Stale quotes surface via `python -m graph receipts`; the gate
  refuses a quote its source does not contain.
  Receipts are review evidence — canonize deliberately never renders
  them into files.
- Before authoring any claim's sentence into canon, verify it against
  the source's CURRENT bytes — a sealed reading ages, and sentences
  authored from a stale one regress canon that has already moved on.
- NEVER write derived edge types (INSTANCE_OF, projections, MENTIONS,
  lift edges, KNOWN_AT…) or machine labels (Archetype/Step/Outcome) —
  the delta lint rejects them with the reason.
- **Identity stays single-label; membership is multi.** Each citizen is
  keyed and exported by exactly one roster label — its home, its
  catalog, its source — and that never changes. But a citizen may be
  declared a member of more than one concept: author a ground
  `DECLARED_MEMBER_OF` edge FROM the citizen TO a Concept Archetype,
  carrying a required `basis` rationale, and derivation folds it into
  the citizen's `INSTANCE_OF`. So a gem its roster makes a Treasure can
  ALSO be declared a Tool while a sibling gem on the same roster is not
  — an overlap no longer needs the shared-catalog-vocabulary workaround.
  The
  edge only ADDS membership and never re-homes the citizen: its
  target is any Concept-rooted subject — a plain concept, or a label
  row that is also a concept (a home with a catalog can be a subject
  too, so a sword kind may be declared Equipment while every sword
  keeps its home) — never a Facet or a Provenance-rooted row; the
  target may be born by the same round; and `INSTANCE_OF` itself
  stays never-authored — the fold computes it.
- A concept Archetype born by THIS round's schema edit does not exist
  in scratch (scratch is cut pre-schema from the backup) — anchor
  Judgment ABOUT edges for brand-new labels to value citizens instead.
  The same constraint blocks DOMAIN ground edges: an edge whose target
  citizen is born by this round's schema edit cannot be authored in
  scratch at all. Declare exactly those edges in the round's STITCH
  file — `graph/proposals/current/stitch.json`, a JSON list of
  connections in the proposal document's edge shape (type, from_label,
  from_name, to_label, to_name, optional props). They ride the same
  approval and land in the same apply, after re-derivation births
  their endpoints; the delta report itemizes them under "Stitch" and
  refuses any that don't genuinely need it. Never re-point a deferred
  edge at a lesser endpoint that happens to exist. (Marker-row
  deferrals from earlier rounds still land at the opening move; new
  rounds use the stitch.)
- Provenance URLs on Judgment rows: take the repo from `gh repo view`,
  never guess the owner (a guessed owner once landed in a whole batch
  of rows and forced a correction round).

### 5. Delta + self-review (agent + machine)
`python -m graph delta` — the itemized, linted changeset
(graph/reports/delta.md). Read it against your own plan: every
surprise is either fixed in scratch or demoted to the uncertain bucket.
Lint violations are yours to fix before the approver ever sees the
report. Then `python -m graph canonize` (dry run) — confirm everything
renders deterministically; a REVIEW-REQUIRED item at this stage means a
schema ruling was missed: go back to step 3 (or the plan gate if it is a
genuinely new decision).

### 6. The diff gate (the approver)
Present the delta report — and offer the Bloom walk on scratch (the
proposal is explorable as a graph before it exists in canon). The
approver resolves the uncertain bucket: rule, "give it a go" (back to
step 4), or park as Judgment citizens. Approval here is approval of the
exact changeset.

**Mid-round refactor pressure is never round scope.** A tempting
rename, a structural cleanup the round doesn't need — park it as a
Judgment row routed via HAS_DISCIPLINE / HAS_AUDIENCE to the project's
Discipline and Audience citizens. The kernel declares those two
classes only; each project's values are its own, disclosed by the team
or discerned from real cases — the first round that needs a value
proposes it at the escalation gate like any new vocabulary. Parked
pressure is design input for a later phase, never scope creep.

### 7. Approve, canonize + drain to zero (machine)
When the approver rules "approved" at the diff gate, record it:
`python -m graph approve` (the record names the human; the proposal's
content hash is frozen — apply replays exactly what was reviewed, and
refuses by name if scratch or the base moved after approval). Then
`python -m graph canonize --apply` — GRAPH-NATIVE since the flip:
no file is edited. Apply verifies the live database still
matches the backup, applies the pinned changeset to the ground layer,
re-derives every machine layer, loads canon, re-exports the backup FROM
the database, and writes the EVENT LOG (chained entry in
`graph/proposals/applied.log` + the delta's inverse) — all one command,
refusing collated and writing nothing on any failure. Then the ritual:
pytest → commit the export + round archive + applied.log line in one
change set. The next round cuts scratch fresh
(`python -m graph restore --database scratch`). The bootstrap-era verbs are retired; `restore`
rebuilds any database from the committed backup.

### 8. Bookkeeping (same standards as any round)
Judgment rows for parked items (they can flow through scratch + canonize
too), the ontology TODO block, the glossary stage (classify every
unresolved-term hit; shrink the stub worklist), skills updated with any
lesson learned in-session — **stated timelessly and domain-neutrally**:
no issue numbers, no dates, no project vocabulary; the rule stands on
its own, with an agnostic example where one earns its keep. PR
provenance lands via the NEXT round's standing opening move (step 4) —
the shipped PR's link cannot exist before ship, so the stamp is always
one round behind by design. Definition
of Done applies: tests, docs, skills ride along.


- **Conferral is declared, never automatic.** A kind's parentage does
  not hold universally over its members (the spiked boot is a weapon;
  most boots are not), so membership climbs the taxonomy only where
  the kind's own `SUBTYPE_OF` link carries `confers: true` — canon
  content the gate reads, hop by hop: an unmarked link stops the
  climb. A member that is the exception declines the parent with its own
  connection — `(member)-[:DECLINES_CONFERRAL]->(concept)`,
  member-grained (the citizen is not that thing by conferral,
  whichever membership raised the question), carrying its own required
  `basis`. The owner's standing law, verbatim: "no embedded lists" — a
  plural fact is connections, never a packed string. The gate speaks both sides aloud: a conferring
  link announces what the member becomes and names the decline road; an
  unmarked link asks the intent question and names the
  direct-declaration road. Nothing confers unstated.

## The flow

1. **Cut the target's working copy fresh.** `python -m graph restore --database <copy>`
   for canon, or `restore --from graph/branches/<name>/export --database <name>-scratch`
   for a Pocket Universe. The merge wants a copy that equals its base, so what
   lands is exactly the rounds taken up plus the owner's rulings; a copy
   that already differs refuses by name.
2. **Prepare the merge.** `python -m graph merge --from <line> --into <line>`
   (`canon` or a Pocket Universe's name on either side). The source's rounds since
   the fork are read from its archived proposals — code carries values.
   A citizen or connection touched by
   only one side is DISJOINT and replays mechanically into the copy
   through the same applier every round rides — a source round's
   declared moves replay with it, ride the prepared round under the
   approval's hash, and land first at apply, itemized at the gate as
   the ceremony move lines they are; one changed on both lines is CONTESTED — left at the
   target's version and listed base / yours / theirs in
   `graph/reports/merge-report.json`, with the merge record riding the
   round as `merge.json`. Rounds already taken up by an earlier merge
   are skipped; a round with no changeset (a derived-layer refresh) is
   noted and skipped.
3. **Rule the contested citizens** by ordinary authoring in the copy —
   the front door presents each with base, yours, theirs, and a
   recommendation; the owner rules; the agent carries judgment, never
   the verb. A contested citizen left untouched lands the target's
   version, knowingly: `delta` names every one as an advisory.
4. **Land it as any round.** `delta` → the diff gate → `approve` →
   `canonize --apply`. The target's log gains a merged-from annotation
   naming the rounds taken up, so a second merge skips them and
   succession's divergence advisory no longer lists rounds that already
   rode across.

name: front-door
description: Be the designer-facing voice over every job — render approval gates, answer questions, take in artifacts, hold debate threads — in the designer's own language, learned live from canon. Use whenever the human in the room is the world's designer (not an engineer working on the machinery): presenting a pending changeset, answering "what is X / what connects to X", receiving any artifact for ingestion, or debating a ruling. The jobs (graph-query, agentic-intake, generation) run underneath; this skill governs everything the designer sees.
---

# The front door

The door is a separate concept from the jobs it invokes. It owns the
only conversation the designer sees; the jobs own the work. Its
constitution is the fifteen tenets in the engine's front-door-tenets
design record — `python -m graph docs front-door-tenets` — read
them before speaking. This skill
is the operating procedure that puts them into practice.

**The invariant:** the door never parses prose for facts and never
speaks machinery words. Facts come from two places only — the typed
records the jobs emit, and canon itself, queried LIVE: through the
query-only read path, never a peek at the committed backup (the
backup serves round mechanics and drills, not answers). A canon
claim in any answer or gate presentation carries its QUERY
RECEIPT — the query run and what it returned. If a fact is not in
a record and not in canon, the door does not know it, and says so
(T14).

## The invariants (medium-independent)

1. **Facts come from provenance, only.** Every asserting element — a
   number, a name, a relationship, a depicted attribute — must trace to
   a citizen, or on a cold graph to the source artifact itself. If
   neither holds anything, that is a GAP surfaced to the owner as a
   question, never filled by invention.
2. **Steering shapes presentation, never facts.** Steering that would
   contradict canon gets surfaced, not silently obeyed.
3. **Nothing semantically omitted or distorted** within the request's
   scope; presentation free inside that boundary.
4. **The raw ask + context ride verbatim** into every brief. Derived
   context supplements, never replaces.

name: rebuild-graph
description: Restore, re-derive, validate, and verify the canon Neo4j graph. Use after a schema-bootstrap edit, when a database looks stale or drifted, when the golden test fails, or when a human asks to reload/refresh/reset the graph.
---

# The maintenance loop

Boundary context: `python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine`

The graph is canon (the flip); `graph/export/` is its committed backup,
written FROM the database. Source files (CSVs, overlays) are bootstrap
scaffolding and may legitimately lag canon. The verbs, by situation:

1. `python -m graph restore` — rebuild the live database from the
   committed backup alone (no sources involved). DRILL PASSED means the
   database re-serializes byte-identical to the backup. This is the
   reset for a stale or drifted live database, and the routine
   reconcile step after a merge.
2. `python -m graph restore --database scratch` — cut a fresh round:
   scratch becomes a clone of canon with the base pinned. Run it before
   any scratch authoring and after any schema edit.
3. A schema concern is a ceremony round — the retired from-sources
   `validate` verb refuses by name, and the health verbs below are
   every corpus's check.
4. `python -m graph rederive` — the derived-layer refresh after an
   engine change that moved a derive pass, or a ceremony that reshaped
   the schema: re-derives the machine layers over the unchanged ground
   facts against the schema the graph itself carries. Dry run by
   default — it prints what leaves and arrives, the report the owner
   rules on; `--apply` performs the refresh as a first-class round
   (anchor stamped, backup re-exported, the record chained into the
   event log and archived). It refuses, collated, if the event log
   disagrees with the backup, if the schema has errors, or if ground
   facts would change — ground changes go through the delta path,
   never through derivation.
5. **Backup coherence is enforced**: any change that alters the graph
   must re-export the backup in the same change set — the golden test
   (`tests/test_golden.py`) proves the backup's derived layers agree
   with what `derive()` recomputes. A golden failure after an
   intentional change isn't an error; it's the reminder.
6. `make check` — canned consistency checks
   (`graph/cypher/checks/*.cypher`) against the live DB. Two species:
   checks headed `// expect: empty` are ASSERTIONS — rows mean an
   integrity bug and the command exits non-zero. The rest are FINDING
   REPORTS — rows are open data questions (candidate Judgments),
   informational by design. A failed assertion blocks; findings never
   do.
7. Spot-verify via MCP (counts per label, a known query from the
   cookbook).

`make test` runs the full pytest suite. The bootstrap-era verbs
(`load`, `validate`, `export --from-sources`) are retired: each
refuses by name and points at the graph-native path.

Every one of these verdicts also lands as a record beside its prose, under `graph/reports/`: the drill writes `restore-report.json`, the checks `check-report.json`, the corpus re-check `corpus-report.json`, the seal handshake `seal-report.json`, the receipt sweep `receipts-report.json`, the answer-key sweep `answer-keys-report.json`, the dependency drift query `dependencies-report.json` (every pinned dependency against what its checkout holds — held, behind, or unreachable; exit 1 on any trouble, so a later tool can alert), and the round-trip scorecard `roundtrip-report.json` beside `roundtrip.md` — one row per thing checked, held rows included, each carrying a verdict code and its plain-language ref, reflecting the latest run. The screen says what it always said; the record says the same thing to anything that reads records.

## The trace and the margin

- Every run records who was cast, what they were told, what they
  cited, what the judge ruled, what escalated. Claims about runs cite
  the trace; recollection is not a source.
- The trace machinery is the engine's runs module (graph.runs): open with new_run(brief,
  started), record judgments with add_row (question / answer /
  decision / opinion — decided_by names the agent, confidence graded
  honestly), and file the archive with write_archive under graph/runs/
  at run end. Ratifying a row into canon goes through the ordinary
  approval ceremony; promotion(run, name) packages the citation.
- Agent judgments made mid-run (mapping choices, low-confidence calls)
  are Opinions with confidence, kept on the run's record and surfaced
  as MARGIN ANNOTATIONS inline in the presented artifact where
  confidence is low or canon was silent. The owner replies in the same
  margin; an owner catch on an UNFLAGGED decision means confidence was
  miscalibrated — record it.
- Annotations anchor to (artifact, span) from day one. The machinery
  is the engine's runs module: pass anchor={artifact, start, end, text} to
  add_row (the exact quote is mandatory — it re-locates the span if
  the artifact moves); margin(run, fingerprint, artifact_text) reads
  the floor census in span order; render_margin presents artifact and
  annotations together; write_archive(run, dir, artifacts) refuses
  any anchor whose quote is not really in its artifact.
- Before saying "done" after any fix round, re-check everything the
  owner previously approved — a fix must not silently break prior
  approvals; a defect class the owner caught once is checked by
  machine thereafter. The machinery is `python -m graph corpus`
  (the engine's corpus module; the KB keeps its ledger at graph/corpus/floors.jsonl): run it
  before any "done" report, and when the owner approves a new
  expectation or catches an unflagged decision, record the floor
  (record_floor: guard test node id, scope, plain-words expectation,
  provenance) in the same change set as the fix.

## What the door never does

- Never invents domain vocabulary, opinions, or design decisions —
  the designer rules; the door informs (T9).
- Never shows machinery words on any surface (T2): no database,
  graph, delta, scratch, round, lint. The system's acts have one
  vocabulary: *enters canon*, *pending your approval*.
- Never presents an item that cannot be ruled on from itself alone
  (T6).
- Never answers without a citation (T11), and never fabricates one:
  an uncitable answer is an absence, said plainly.

## When answering

Lead with the answer, cite counts precisely (say when placeholders are
included/excluded), and if a query surfaces something inconsistent, report it
as a finding — don't fix data unasked.

The check runs at the delta gate when a round touches a key or a checked program's body, and as the DB-free answer-keys sweep. properties.body:
## 1. The Virtues (engine character — any universe)

The Eight Virtues steer the ENGINE, not just any one project [owner: "the
virtues were there to steer any version of the engine/kernel"]. Born in
a project's subject matter, promoted to engine character by the
owner's deliberate act — the promotion doctrine applied to values. A
Z-80 manual or a cookbook project inherits them whole; when they land
on a graph, that is a kernel ceremony with a Decision row.

| Virtue | In the engine, it is… |
|---|---|
| **Honesty** | the honest floor; traces over recollection; confidence honestly stated |
| **Compassion** | meet the user where they are: deduce their meaning, convert their format, never make them redo work; plain language always |
| **Valor** | escalate with work shown; surface the unwelcome finding, including against yourself |
| **Justice** | fair adjudication: conflict-preserving merges, minority reports never averaged away, every verdict traceable |
| **Sacrifice** | the machine absorbs cost and failure so the human doesn't |
| **Honour** | integrity of the record: the chained log, kept inverses, refusing the expedient fake |
| **Spirituality** | the system examining itself: retros, calibration, the regression corpus |
| **Humility** | assist, never one-shot; the right-sized model for the job; knowing the machine's place |

None of these entries is aspirational: each names machinery that
already shipped. The character was in the code before it had names.

properties.body:
## 2. The Tenets (ruled by the owner; wording remains his)

**Of Honesty**
1. An honest red beats a faked green.
2. Nothing lost, nothing invented, nothing distorted — presentation is
   free. *(the parity doctrine, verbatim; already a Decision row)*
3. The record is the source; recollection is not.

**Of Compassion**
4. Meet the user where they are: deduce their meaning, convert their
   format, never make them redo work.
5. Plain language is the interface; jargon stops at the machinery's
   edge.

**Of Valor**
6. Escalation is showing your work, not confessing failure.
7. Surface the unwelcome finding — including against yourself.

**Of Justice**
8. Disagreement is data: preserve the minority, cite every voice,
   never pre-average.
9. What the system understands is declared and ruled — never folklore,
   never string-luck.

**Of Sacrifice**
10. The machine absorbs cost and failure so the human doesn't.

**Of Honour**
11. Every claim cites its provenance; an expert that cannot cite is
    roleplay.
12. The record is never rewritten — corrected forward, with inverses
    kept.

**Of Spirituality**
13. Every catch becomes a check: the system turns its failures into
    guards on itself.

**Of Humility**
14. The machine gets out of the way until stakes summon it.

**Universal** *(serving the whole stack; tenets need not map 1:1 to a
Virtue [owner])*
15. Consent binds to mutation, not completion.
16. Ceremony is a floor for the machine, never a ceiling on
    conversation.
17. Born ephemeral, promoted by evidence.

The Universal section is also structural: new tenets land here first
and map to a Virtue only if one claims them — tenet 17 applied to the
tenet list itself.

properties.body:
## 3. The Method (the owner's ten steps — wording WIP, his to strike)

The order of operations. Run as the orchestrator's HABITS — internal on
every ask, surfacing to the human only when an answer is genuinely
missing [customer; pragmatist; owner] — never as gated states the
customer tours.

1. Understand the ask; confirm only what is genuinely ambiguous,
   batched into one asking — missing understanding escalates, with
   work shown.
2. Understand the audience — including which archetype is asking: a
   resident collaborator or a drop-and-go customer.
3. Understand the artifacts at play — their Units (which axes, what
   hierarchy), their provenance state (warm canon or cold source), and
   their standing disambiguations (examples, forward references,
   ladder directions).
4. Understand the person — their persistent steering, their named
   blind spots — and how this ask fits what came before.
5. Understand how the results should be organized (the artifact's
   composition: which elements, arranged how).
6. Understand the presentation desired (the audience-facing form).
   Work DECOMPOSITION — how the job shards — is not a step of its own:
   it is derived from 5 and 6 [owner: the composition disentangling].
7. Only now does the work begin — but understanding is a habit, not a
   hallway: an unambiguous ask spends zero of the customer's time
   getting here.
8. Review before presenting: judge first where a judge exists,
   re-check everything previously approved, and name-and-classify
   whatever remains — the honest floor.
9. Present whole, with the margin attached — the system's own flagged
   doubts alongside the work — and deduce what kind of judgment each
   reply is; never demand a format.
10. Get consent where it binds: whatever changes recorded truth or
    publishes. A read-only answer completes by being answered.

properties.body:
## 4. The architecture: a short path plus engagement signals

v1's pipeline is inverted [all five critics, converging]: every ask
runs a FOUR-STOP default path, and heavier machinery ENGAGES only when
a signal demands it.

```
  DEFAULT PATH (every ask)

  UNDERSTAND-AS-HABIT ──> WORK ──> FLOOR + PRESENT ──> ITERATE/CONSENT
   Method 1–6 internal;    one agent,  honest floor,      margin loop;
   ONE gate, only when     brief +     whole artifact,    consent binds
   ambiguous or mutating   judge loop  trace attached     to MUTATION

  ENGAGEMENT SIGNALS — each brings machinery in when true:
  · no deterministic judge for this artifact → critique ensemble
  · generator is mute (single-shot)          → composition ensemble
  · units > 1 declared                       → shard + coherence expert
  · worker and judge disagree repeatedly     → second opinion / panel
  · canon mutation or publication at stake   → gate + consent tighten
  · stuck anywhere                           → escalate, work shown

  PARK-AND-RESUME: a stuck, blocked, or disconnected run parks with
  its floor census — it never deadlocks and never self-completes.
  [operator FATAL: deadlock at spent-budget + absent owner; the v1
  "one 7b per run" budget is deleted as numerology [refuter]]
```

- Critique-ensemble weight scales inversely with deterministic-
  evaluator strength [kept from v1; evidence-backed].
- The composition habit owns the UNIT question on every ask: which
  axes (structural / temporal / spatial), what hierarchy; "none" and
  "sequence-of" are legal answers, "cannot tell" escalates. Units is a
  standing question BECAUSE the owner self-reports forgetting it —
  owner-named blind spots become standing habits; Units is the first
  case. [owner] When units > 1, casting auto-adds a cross-unit
  coherence expert [refuter: survives refutation for documents].
- The base case stands: plan generation is one seeded casting step,
  never a meta-ensemble [kept from v1, uncontested].

[customer FATAL: two archetypes hid in one machine; owner: ruled, with

properties.body:
## 7. Evaluability: traces, the run graph, and the regression corpus

[operator FATAL: no run-trace; historian FATAL: no way to show any
future version is better; refuter: four author claims in v1's own
evidence appendix were untraceable to the record — confirmed]

- **Every run emits a trace**: who was cast, what they were told, what
  they cited, what the judge ruled, what escalated. Claims about runs
  cite traces; recollection is not a source.
- **The trace is a run-scoped judgment graph** [owner]: Question /
  Answer / Decision nodes with decided_by: <agent>, scoped to the run,
  archived beside it at run end (inspectable forever, canon never) and
  discarded from the working set. Precedent: the judging machinery's
  per-artifact workspace database. Agent judgments are OPINIONS with
  confidence (made a kernel class) until the owner ratifies one — ratification
  promotes it to a durable, owner-authority Judgment row through the
  normal ceremony. Born ephemeral, promoted by ruling. Implemented:
  graph/runs.py — pure-logic build, JSONL archive under
  graph/runs/<run-id>/, and a promotion helper whose package cites the
  run id and nothing archive-internal (canon survives archive loss).
  Span anchors implemented: judgments carry (artifact
  fingerprint, start, end, quoted text) — the quote re-locates the
  span when the artifact moves; margin() reads an artifact's anchored
  judgments in span order and render_margin presents them in place;
  archiving with artifact bytes refuses quotes that are not there.
- **Canon attribution closes the triangle** (owner-ruled): parity
  proves draft ≡ original; attribution
  (graph/attribution.py, wired into the roundtrip scorecard and the
  whole-book unit `roundtrip --book`) proves draft ⊆ canon on a graded
  source ladder — structured properties, carried receipts, long-prose
  homes (the soup rung, attributed AND a named debt). A homeless claim
  splits on parity: original says it → CANON GAP (auto-debt, shipping
  never stops at any density); parity called it invented →
  UNATTRIBUTED INVENTION (presented with the artifact, named red,
  never hidden). Citations are strong-form: earned only when the
  cited citizen is in the drafter's trace-recorded consulted set;
  unearned-but-correct re-derives invisibly. Inputs are layered: the
  original and any finding quoting it are evaluator-internal;
  generator feedback is redacted to defect-class + citizen pointers.
  The original remains the parity reference until the owner EXPLICITLY
  declares succession — no milestone implies it. Attribution and
  ingestion are one mapping machinery in two directions; intake runs
  sealed-then-mapping (the pocket-universe phasing; the visibility
  system that will enforce the seal physically is designed and built
  at [lenses.md](lenses.md) — the seal rides as discipline
  until the declarations take graph residence at the owner's gate).
- **The regression corpus**: owner-approved floors are re-checked
  before any "done" — a fix cannot silently break prior approvals, and
  the second occurrence of a defect class is caught before the owner
  sees it. First-of-class remains the owner's catch, honestly.
  Implemented: graph/corpus.py + the committed ledger
  graph/corpus/floors.jsonl — one floor per approval (guard test node,
  scope, expectation in plain words, provenance), `python -m graph
  corpus` re-checks all of them, and a deleted or renamed guard reds
  as "the guard is gone" naming the approval it orphaned.
- Critique panels police themselves: mixed framing (not all
  refutation), inter-rater agreement recorded in the trace, unanimity
  flagged as suspicious rather than celebrated. [historian, applied to
  the very panel that reviewed this document]

properties.body:
## 8. The margin: bidirectional, anchored, deduced

[owner expansion — "annotation is becoming a bigger story"]

- **The system annotates its own output**: low-confidence decisions,
  judgment calls, and uncertainties are flagged inline where they
  occur, each carrying its trace ("chose X; canon silent; looked at
  Y"). This unifies what earlier practice scattered across manifests,
  gaps files, review markers, and agent-proposed confidence grades.
- **The owner replies in the same margin** — ruling on flagged
  decisions, or catching what was NOT flagged. An owner catch on an
  unflagged decision is a calibration miss and feeds the corpus.
- **Classification is deduced, never demanded** [owner]: users just
  comment; the system deduces defect / taste / question, and the
  deduction is itself a run-scoped Opinion with confidence.
  [O]/[S]/[Q] survives as internal spine and power-user shorthand.
- **Anchoring from day one** [owner]: every annotation references
  (artifact, span) — the margin is a graph of span→judgment pairs. The
  future UI overlay (dialogue with the artifact directly, instead of
  or beside the text input) is a renderer over the same run graph;
  nothing remodels when the UI arrives.
- The floor census IS the collected margin, read in place.

## 9. Superseded: what v1 got wrong, and who killed it

- The ten-state pipeline: ceremony-by-default with opt-outs; a simple
  query cost ~12 customer touches [customer, with step counts].
- The cast-diff gate: never run, reviewed topology while defects lived
  in briefs, blind to a wrong seed, rubber-stamp economics
  [pragmatist, refuter, operator, historian — four independent kills].
- The one-7b adjudication budget: asserted, not derived; deadlocked at
  owner absence [refuter, operator]. Replaced by park-and-resume.
- Mandatory composition ensembles: inverted the campaign's only
  composition finding [refuter]; survives only as the mute-generator
  signal, whose first live test is the owner's portrait request.

## A self-world, riding the engine's own version

The engine's knowledge base lives in this repo (`manual/`) and is a
world like any the engine serves — its own canon, its own project
ontology grown through gated rounds, its own chained event log — with
one deliberate difference: **it has no version of its own.** Its
rounds land on this repo's main; a release tag freezes code and canon
together; the packaged export ships inside the wheel the way the
metaontology seed does. A consuming world that pins engine X therefore
gets the conduct and doctrine of X by construction — one pin, no
second version to resolve, no compatibility matrix. Conduct is
documentation of the machinery it operates; desynchronizing them is
the failure mode, not the flexibility.

It is ruled a *self*-world: it moves atomically with engine changes in
the same change set, so it does not count toward the
multiple-consuming-worlds thresholds elsewhere in the doctrine —
though it does, over time, furnish the second-project evidence that
kernel promotions await.

Keeping code and record in step is conduct, not calendar: a change
that moves behavior a design or conduct record describes updates
that record's canon in the same ship — the way tests, docs, and
skills ride every change — and a plan gate that opens a new
subsystem (new kernel concepts, a new job class) names where its
story will live: a section of an existing record, or a new record
whose first round rides the ship. A record found stale is a defect
to fix, never a chore to schedule.

# Agentic ETL — the Persistent-Graph Era

*** DESIGN DOCUMENT — REQUIRES DESIGNER REVIEW ***

The successor architecture to the derived-graph ETL. One paragraph: **the
proposal is a graph, review is a graph walk, verification is a query, and
the only code is a fixed micro-kernel that never grows.** Agents author
ground facts directly in a scratch graph — *scratch for now*: whether
isolation in the end means a branch of the live graph, a lock,
or a temporal mechanism is the open decision below, and everything else
in this design survives any of those answers. The reviewable artifact is
the **delta**; canonization is deterministic replay of an approved delta;
the delta is the event-log entry; derived layers are never authored by
anyone. No code is ever generated.

This document is the review surface: a twin-track narrative (what the
submitter experiences / what happens under the hood), the process state
machine, the delta lifecycle, and the open isolation decision.

## Anatomy of a delta

A delta is **comprehensive** — the complete, itemized mutation set, every
class enumerated so full roll-back is always possible:

1. Nodes to create
2. Existing nodes to edit (per-property before → after)
3. Existing nodes to delete
4. Edges to create
5. Existing edges to edit (per-property before → after)
6. Existing edges to delete
7. Any other mutation class the schema grows (the list is closed per
   delta, never implicit)

**Derived edges are shadows, not itemized removals.** A machine-computed
edge (an INSTANCE_OF, a signature projection) never enters the list as a
bare deletion — it is a shadow of the ground-fact change that re-derives
it, so deleting a node is never blocked by the computed edges hanging off
it (re-derivation owns them at apply). Authored derived-edge *additions*
and paired modifications still itemize, so the lint can refuse them and
the diff-gate reader sees every consequence.

Every entry records its **inverse** (the before-image), which is what
makes the event log reversible. Every entry carries its receipt, source
pointer, and authority grade. Every member is **tagged with the delta's
id** — this is what lets exploration tools isolate "just the proposal."

One mutation class is **distinguished above all others**: changes to the
graph's own schema layers — the embedded ontology and metaontology
citizens. These have the biggest echoes: a project-schema edit can
re-derive edges across the whole graph, and a kernel (metaontology) edit
is ceremony by doctrine. The delta therefore classifies schema-layer
mutations into their own section, presented FIRST at the diff gate, with
a blast-radius summary ("this schema change re-derives 214 edges across 6
labels") — you should never discover a schema edit by stumbling over it
among row-level facts.

Three more things ride inside the delta document itself:

- **Declared moves** — a rename of the world's own label or concept,
  or a re-homing of named citizens under a kind of what they were —
  ride beside the changeset, embedded in the proposal so the
  approval hash covers them. The gate itemizes each move with its
  counts and refusals; when moves rode, the recorded inverse is the
  FULL ground diff — the only honest walk-back for a relabel.

- **The implications narrative** — a prose explanation of what the change
  *means*, in crisp human-comprehensible statements with concrete
  examples pulled from the corpus wherever possible ("The Cinder Fox now
  guards the Hollow Gem: a reader asking what the Fox protects gets the
  Gem…"). Written for a person, not a parser; reviewed at the diff gate
  alongside the itemized list.
- **The delta's tests** — generated regression checks that ride with the
  change (new `.cypher` invariants, answer-key assertions where a fact
  table overlaps). They run at verification, run again at apply, and then
  join the permanent suite — the persistent-era form of "tests ride with
  the feature." Tests are data, not code; the kernel's check-runner never
  grows.

The delta is **live through the gates**: every human-in-the-loop
course-correction at the plan or diff gate updates it in place — what you
approve is always the current delta, and approval is what freezes it
(hash-pinned; any change after that is a new delta).

## Born graph-native

The engine's corpus is the first knowledge base **born graph-native**:
`python -m graph init` seeds a committed backup holding the kernel's
schema stratum alone — no bootstrap schema file, no sources, no derive path,
the same seed shape a schema-only branch cut is born from. Everything
else grows through ordinary gated rounds. The project layer starts
empty, so its first growth is **label births** riding the schema
ceremony ([ontology-doctrine.md](ontology-doctrine.md)); prose
citizens carry their bodies on the graph and their containment
re-derives from declared linking props — the section machinery with no
source file anywhere.

A corpus born this way carries zero YAML and never acquires any —
and since the from-sources era closed, every knowledge base is
born this way.
## Boundary rules

---

The tenets are domain-agnostic and travel with the engine, like the
intake conduct before them. The machinery's own reports — the typed
records and the technical rendering — are unchanged underneath; the
door is a reader of records and canon, never a second source of
truth.

The tenets are the same everywhere; the door is not. Each world's
door is expected to be **tailored to that world's experience**: the
conduct trunk ships with the engine at whatever version the world
pins, the voice is learned live from that world's canon (T1), and a
world keeps its own local skills beside the engine's. Two worlds at
different pins run different conduct on purpose — skew is a chosen
consequence of pinning ([engine-as-corpus.md](engine-as-corpus.md)).
## Conduct

## Dependencies: reaching another knowledge base A world knows which knowledge bases it uses by declaring them. A **[Knowledge Base Dependency]** is a citizen of the declaring KB — the almanac, named in the declarer's own terms, pinned to an edition (the dependency's committed-backup identity and its event-log sequence) with an intent, read or write. A **[Citizen Bookmark]** reaches one citizen of that dependency — by the label and name the dependency's own canon uses, and the edition it was resolved against — and states which dependency it resolves in (exactly one RESOLVES_IN). The declaring KB's own citizens then point at the bookmark through their own relation vocabulary: the bookmark is the declared crossing, and nothing in one KB silently points into another. WHERE a dependency actually lives is settings, not canon: the declaring KB's environment names a path per dependency (`GHOSTWHEEL_DEPENDENCY_=`), so the same canon serves two machines whose checkouts live in different places. Resolution reads the dependency's own committed backup at that path — code carries values; nothing queries another knowledge base's live database. `python -m graph dependencies` is the ruler: every declared dependency and bookmark judged against what its checkout actually holds — held, behind (the checkout differs from the pin), or unreachable — one row per verdict in the report beside the prose, exit nonzero on any trouble so a later tool can alert. A clean pass says so, row by row: a non-event is still read aloud. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph MACHINE["one shared DBMS - the stamps are its registry"] RC["rules canon
stamp: kb rules"] RS["rules-scratch
stamp: working copy"] BC["almanac canon
stamp: kb almanac"] end subgraph RULES["the rules KB"] DEP["[Knowledge Base Dependency]
the almanac - edition - intent"] BM["[Citizen Bookmark]
a creature, by label + name"] ENV["settings:
GHOSTWHEEL_DEPENDENCY_ALMANAC = path"] end BM -- RESOLVES_IN --> DEP DEP -- "resolved at the path, from
the committed backup" --> BC ENV -.- DEP ```

## Depiction, interpretation, and what opens it **DEPICTS** names the artifact's objective contents — one edge per thing shown, medium-neutral: a song depicts a horn as surely as a picture does. Each pairing carries a ROLE: `primary` — the blessed reference assignment — or `also-shows`, an inventory fact one hop away ("find me images of shields"); a pairing with no role is a plain fact. Every primary pairing derives its boilerplate interpretation in the same round that stages it — "X as Y reference", the machinery's marker on the row, a hand-authored reading always winning its pair — and the gate calls each correlation out while the owner is looking, a second primary reference for one subject included. Depiction claims confirm at the gate; a depicted thing canon does not know is a gate question with two recorded answers — create the citizen here, or ignore it with an [Approved Omission] so a re-scan never re-asks. What the artifact STANDS FOR is an **[Interpretation]**: one per intent, ABOUT exactly one artifact, INTERPRETED_AS its subject, DRAWS_ON only things the artifact depicts. The objective layer and the meaning layer stay separate on purpose — two worlds may read the same picture differently without contesting what it shows. A **[Resolver]** binds a scheme and a location kind to what knows how to open it — OPENS_WITH exactly one [Procedure] or [Citizen Bookmark], so "how do I open this kind of thing?" is canon, not folklore. And an artifact that replaces another says so: the newer SUPERSEDES the older, and the older carries when it was superseded — the marker is the model's; what a world does about what still cites the older one is that world's reading. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["[Artifact]
identity: its name
grade: content held"] N["a newer [Artifact]"] L1["[File Location]
scheme - address - primary
verified fingerprint - sequence - size"] L2["another location kind
rests unverified by design"] T["a thing it shows"] S["what it stands for"] I["[Interpretation]
one per intent"] R["[Resolver]
scheme + location kind"] P["[Procedure] or [Citizen Bookmark]"] A -- LOCATED_AT --> L1 A -- LOCATED_AT --> L2 A -- DEPICTS --> T I -- ABOUT --> A I -- INTERPRETED_AS --> S I -- DRAWS_ON --> T R -- OPENS_WITH --> P N -- SUPERSEDES --> A ```

# Front Door Tenets

The front door is the voice that stands between the designer and the
machinery. It is a separate concept from the jobs it invokes — query,
ingest, generation — and it owns the only conversation the designer
sees: approval gates, questions and answers, ingestion, annotations,
debate. The jobs keep their technical surfaces for agents and
forensics; the door renders everything designer-facing under the
tenets below, settled by owner interview, 2026-08-24 through
2026-08-26.

The reference rendering (a text ingestion in an imaginary world —
the artifact could as well be an image, a model, a song, or a link):

```
COMBAT MANEUVERS — Emberfall · enters canon on your approval · 2 items pending

1. Is Grit also a Combat Skill?

   Your new text treats it that way ("Grit functions as a
   combat skill during rally checks", ¶4); today canon
   knows it only as a Trait. It can be both — canon just
   keeps the why on record, in your words.

   → Tell me why Grit is also a Combat Skill, or tell me
     that sentence shouldn't be read that way.
   ⟨grit · missing-reason⟩

2. Does Rally's definition change?

   Your new text reads: "Rally is the moment, after nerve
   is retested, a routed unit turns to fight." (¶9). Canon's
   current wording: "the moment a routed unit turns to
   fight." Approving makes the after-retest reading explicit
   everywhere Rally is used.

   → Approve the new wording, or keep the current.
   ⟨rally · description-edit⟩

Checked clean: 14 additions, no conflicts.        (ask to see all)
```

## Glossary, for the lay reader

- **Artifact** — anything a person hands the system: a document, a
  table, an image, an audio or video file.
- **Knowledge Base ("KB")** — one body of knowledge as one graph: a
  game's rules could be one KB; a chip's instruction set another that
  someone else publishes and you simply use. Each KB keeps its own
  facts, its own history, and its own approval gate — and its own
  tailoring of the engine's conduct: the trunk ships with the engine
  at the KB's pinned version, and each KB tunes the door's voice
  (learned from its canon) and keeps its own local skills beside it.
- **World** — a context you step INTO that gathers several KBs and
  knows how they relate — nothing is melted together; the world just
  knows which KBs it uses and how to navigate them. (A world is
  itself a KB whose subject is the other KBs.)
- **Branch** — an independent working line inside one KB: your own
  copy with its own history and gate, physically unable to touch the
  real thing, adopted only when the owner ceremonially says so.
- **Canon** — the single shared line of agreed-true facts that
  everyone's work builds on — a KB's main line.
- **Reading room** — the machinery's temporary workspace for
  understanding what was dropped; all artifacts in a submission are
  read into the same room, side by side. Disposable, never part of
  canon.
- **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** — a private playground beside canon:
  your own line of the knowledge base, cut as a copy of canon and
  declared a pocket, readable only by you until you invite someone
  (permissions gate who may *see* the Pocket; the isolation itself
  is the line). Canon cannot be touched from inside it; merge
  carries its work to canon's ordinary gate when you choose, exit
  and your view returns to canon, discard and nothing anywhere
  happened. (A pocket spanning a whole world — one bundle across
  its KBs — is the designed next rung.)
- **Proposal** — a bundled set of changes to canon, frozen so that what
  gets approved is exactly what gets applied.
- **Plan gate** — the first conversation: "here's how I read your
  artifact — did I read it right?"
- **Diff gate** — the second conversation: "here's exactly what would
  change in canon — approve it?"
- **Convergence loop** — the machinery re-checking and re-writing its
  own work until only questions needing human judgment remain.
- **Event log** — the permanent history of every applied change, each
  one undoable.
- **Serve** — answering questions from canon with citations, in the
  medium the evidence lives in, never inventing.

## Glossary, the working vocabulary

*The hardcore definitions — the lay glossary above stays the
gentle entry point. A knowledge base's own domain terms are
not here: they live on the graph itself
(`python -m graph terms`; every citizen carries its own doc)
and in the consuming project's own glossary.*

### The one people ask about first

**Floor** — a promise already made. Two braided uses. The **honest
floor** is the named list of everything still imperfect when work is
presented: remaining defects are classified and shown *with* the work,
never hidden under it — "an honest red beats a faked green." A
**corpus floor** is one owner-approved expectation made durable: the
check that guards it, the expectation in plain words, and the approval
that made it a floor (a PR, a ruling), re-checked by `python -m graph
corpus` before any "done." Work may build *above* a floor; it may
never sink below one, and a floor whose guard vanishes is a loud red,
never a silence.

### Canon and the graph

**Canon** — the Neo4j canon database: the single source of truth
for everything the knowledge base asserts. Files are inputs and backups;
the graph is primary.

**Citizen** — any node that lives in canon. Facts, rulings, procedures,
quotes — if it matters, it's a citizen, queryable and owned.

**Backup / export** — `graph/export/*.jsonl`, written FROM canon,
kept under whatever custody the knowledge base uses (this project
keeps them in git). `restore` rebuilds the database from it alone.

**The drill** — restore from backup, then prove the database
re-serializes byte-identical. Run constantly; "DRILL PASSED" is canon's
heartbeat.

**Ground vs. machine layer** — ground facts are authored (by people or
gated rounds); the machine layer (Archetype nodes, derived edges like
INSTANCE_OF) is *computed* from ground + schema at every apply. Nobody
authors the machine layer; re-derivation owns it.

**Receipts** — review-evidence properties on authored citizens
(`from_text`, `source`, `grade`): the verbatim quote and provenance
that let a claim be checked. Never rendered into outputs.

### The two schema layers

**Metaontology (the kernel)** — the engine's own vocabulary
(`graph/metaontology.yaml`): the four roots (Concept, Facet,
Provenance, Judgment), [Procedure], the Judgment family, the
visibility vocabulary, the artifact family ([Artifact], its
location and interpretation machinery), and the worlds vocabulary
([Knowledge Base Dependency], [Citizen Bookmark], [Pocket
Universe]). Project-agnostic — the membership test is "would a kid's
storybook project need it?" Semver'd; changes are **ceremonies**.

**Project ontology** — everything THIS knowledge base holds as its own
schema: its labels, catalogs, relationships — living ON the graph as
the Archetype stratum. Owner-governed, versioned as a plain revision
number. The from-sources
era is closed: every knowledge base is born graph-native, and
bootstrap files are
archaeology, kept only in the project's own history.

**Ceremony** — the deliberate act of changing the kernel: explicit
owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, the version bump and ledger
line in the same change set. Never casual, never a side effect. The
**schema ceremony** is its project-layer sibling: a closed list of
permitted change classes riding an ordinary gated round, itemized in the delta
report's marked section — approving that round IS the ruling.

**Born graph-native** — a knowledge base seeded from the kernel alone
(`python -m graph init`): no bootstrap files, no sources; its project
layer starts empty and grows through gated rounds.

**Label birth** — the schema-ceremony class that grows an empty
project layer: a new spec-carrying label arriving with its
declaration, permitted only while nothing yet sits underneath it.

### Rounds — how canon changes

**Round** — the unit of canon change: cut scratch → author → delta →
gates → apply. Nothing reaches canon any other way.

**Scratch** — a working database cloned from canon where agents author
freely. Wiped and re-cut per round; mistakes here cost nothing.

**Base pin** — cutting scratch records canon's content identity. If
canon moves mid-round, the apply refuses by name — no round lands on a
base that shifted under it.

**Branch** — an independent line of truth WITHIN a KB: born from a
declared base (schema-only for a rebuild line; clone-of-canon for a
pocket), with its own authoring
copy, ceremony, and chained log, physically unable to write the KB's
live canon, adopted only by the owner's succession ceremony — never a
flag. Pinned base + delta is the contract; the clone is an
implementation detail. A **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** is a branch
cut as a clone of canon and declared a pocket; its work returns
through merge, prepared as the target's ordinary gated round. The
world-level correlation of pockets — one per member KB the work
mutates, read-pins for the rest, landing at one collated gate with
verify-all-before-apply-any extended across every member KB — is
the designed next rung.

**Delta / proposal** — the itemized changeset: scratch minus base,
linted (machine layers refuse authorship), rendered as a report. Its
content hash IS the proposal's identity.

**Plan gate / diff gate** — the two owner gates: the plan gate rules
on intent before authoring; the diff gate rules on the itemized delta
before anything lands. Consent binds to mutation.

**Approve → canonize --apply** — the approval freezes the proposal by
hash; the apply replays exactly that changeset: verify everything
before writing anything, re-derive the machine layer, re-export the
backup, chain the event log.

**Event log & inverse** — one chained, tamper-evident line per applied
round, with the delta's executable inverse recorded — every round can
be walked back.

**Stitch** — the same-round-endpoints mechanism: ground edges whose
target is born by this round's own schema edit ride a declared stitch
file, covered by the same approval, landing after re-derivation births
their endpoints.

**Rederive** — schema-bootstrap maintenance: recompute the machine
layer against the current schema, refusing if ground would change.

**Sitting** — an owner session that rules on a collated sheet of
questions in one pass, rule-by-exception welcome.

**Opening move** — every round's first duty: pay the previous round's
debts (stamp its PR onto its Judgment rows, land its deferred edges).

### The Judgment stratum

**Question / Decision / Answer / Opinion / Requirement / TODO** — the
kernel's ruling vocabulary, all citizens: something open; a ruling made
(by whom, when — supersession expected); a clarification; an agent's
judgment with confidence (junior until ratified); a binding constraint;
work pending. **Approved Omission / Approved Difference** — editorial
rulings the parity judge consults: this absence (or this changed
rendering) is approved and passes forever. **Verbatim** — a passage
pinned to carry word-for-word; the stored bytes are the truth, the
normalized form is only a matching key.

### Quality machinery

**Parity** — the regeneration bar, owner-ruled: nothing lost, nothing
invented, nothing distorted; presentation free. The **judge** compares
claims mechanically and returns verdicts (matched, omitted, invented,
distorted); reds name themselves.

**Attribution** — the other half of the triangle: every claim in a
draft must find its home in canon. **Parity proves draft ≡ original;
attribution proves draft ⊆ canon** — and a claim that passes parity
but has no home is a hole in *canon*, found automatically.

**The ladder (rungs)** — how strong a claim's home is: **first-class**
(a citizen's structured properties, edges, or Step lifts carry the
fact), **receipt** (found in a citizen's carried sentence quotes),
**soup / prose-only** (found only inside long prose — an honest home
AND a named debt). The rung rides the verdict as its confidence.

**Census** — decomposing an artifact into claims and attributing every
one. **Fact grain** — the ruled claim size: one atomic assertion
("Mary gave Arthur an apple" is three claims).

**Soup map** — the census's output read as a debt map: which sections'
facts are structured citizens and which still live as prose blobs.
The prioritized worklist for ingestion.

**Gap vs. invention** — a homeless claim splits on parity: the
original says it → canon gap (a debt; shipping never stops); parity
called it invented → a named red, presented with the artifact, never
hidden. **Phantom gap** — a "gap" the matcher couldn't see was already
home; **laundering** is removing phantoms from the worklist by reading
structure, not just text.

**Corpus** — the ledger of floors (`graph/corpus/floors.jsonl`) plus
the command that re-checks them all; a deleted guard reds as "the
guard is gone," naming the approval it orphaned.

**Tripwire** — a test that exists to refuse a specific forgetting: the
schema-version ledger, the roster check, the vocabulary leak. When a
tripwire reds, it worked.

### Runs and margins

**Run / trace** — one casting of agents against a brief, its record
kept as a run-scoped judgment graph: who was cast, what they were
told, what they consulted, what they judged. Claims about runs cite
traces; recollection is not a source.

**Margin** — the system's own annotations on an artifact, span-anchored
(the quote re-locates if the text moves): low-confidence calls,
uncertainties, questions. The owner replies in the same margin; the
reply threads to the Opinion it answers.

**Earned citation** — strong-form attribution: a citation counts when
the cited citizen appears in the drafter's trace. Right-answer-wrong-
path re-derives invisibly.

**Park, never die** — a blocked or interrupted run keeps its state and
resumes; the owner never has to say "try again."

### Lenses — who sees what

**Visibility Class** — a named set of graph elements; the only unit
permissions speak about. Kind **knowledge** (assume-deny: hidden
unless granted) or **masking** (assume-allow: removed only when a mask
names it).

**Visibility Group** — a subject of sight; individuals are size-1
groups; groups nest. (Named "Visibility Group" because a knowledge
base may need the plain word "Group" for its own domain.)

**Verdict** — an authored ALLOWED or DENIED between a group and a
class; denies target flat classes only.

**Fold / lens** — the fold is a subject's transitive group set; the
lens is that fold compiled into what they may see, enforced on the
in-memory graph itself so edges never dangle and derived layers
recompute under it. **Activation** — wearing a subset of your groups
this session; exiting a Pocket is a lens subtraction, not a
membership edit.

**Super admin** — no lens applied. Not a subject with every grant — the
absence of filtering.

**Redacted refusal** — the subject-facing answer for anything hidden:
one uniform "Nothing by that name that you can see." Candid
explanations are a curator privilege.

**Sealed reading** — intake's first phase: comprehend the artifact on
its own terms (kernel allowed, project canon forbidden) before any
mapping, so canon can't bias the reading. **Mapping phase** — then
each artifact-local claim is judged against canon: same-as / extends /
new / contradicts, every mapping a recorded Opinion.

### Campaign terms

**Re-ingest** — the declared milestone: rebuild canon clean from the
published knowledge base, rulings carried, the census as the ruler.

**Succession** — the original remains the parity reference until
the owner *explicitly* declares otherwise. No milestone implies it.

**Wave** — one gated slice of a campaign, sized by the worklist,
closed at a diff gate.

## Identity is the name; location is a row

An **[Artifact]** is the thing itself, as canon knows it: its identity
is its NAME — a stable handle in the world's own words — never a path.
WHERE it is lives on **[Artifact Location]** rows behind LOCATED_AT,
each carrying a scheme, an address, and whether it is the primary
copy; an artifact has exactly one primary. Copies move, get renamed,
appear in second places; the artifact stays one citizen and its
locations are rows that come and go.

**[File Location]** is the kernel's own location kind — the one the
engine natively resolves, reads, and verifies. A world may declare
further location kinds under [Artifact Location] through the ordinary
taxonomy ceremony; a location of a kind the engine cannot read rests
unverified by design, stated plainly rather than guessed at.

## Invariants (the non-negotiables)

1. **The structural write boundary.** The agent's write credentials exist
   only for scratch. The live connection is physically query-only —
   separate database, separate auth, not a settings-file politeness. The
   agent holding a pen near canon is the one failure mode with no machine
   net under it. *Real: the live connection rides a query-only reader
   user (read-only on canon, scratch not even visible); a write attempt
   dies at the database with Forbidden. The settings-file deny remains as
   the second belt.*
2. **Derived layers are never authored** — by agent, human, or tool.
   Ground facts in, derivations recomputed. An agent-emitted INSTANCE_OF
   is asserted-signature drift at graph scale (the lesson the engine paid
   for in the derived era, generalized).
3. **Only approved artifacts touch canon**, and approval pins by hash.
   The applier replays exactly what was approved or nothing.
4. **Preconditions at apply, detection over cleverness.** Base drift
   kicks back with the conflict named; the applier never merges
   creatively.
5. **Receipts are properties, verification is a join.** Every non-obvious
   ground fact carries `from_text`; source docs are Provenance citizens;
   the receipts check is a graph query, not a file grep.
6. **Two human gates for a mutating intake**: plan (before authoring),
   diff (before canonization). These two gates ARE the agentic approach's
   two engagement signals instantiated ([agentic-approach.md](agentic-approach.md)):
   the plan gate is the collated-ambiguity interview, the diff gate is the
   mutation consent. An intake trips both signals every time — it always
   disambiguates and always mutates — so it always has both gates; a
   read-only query trips neither and has none. Everything between the two
   gates is agent + kernel loops that never need you.

## Names on a shared machine

A knowledge base has a name: the one its canon declares on its own
anchor, or, until it declares one, the name of the directory it lives
in. Declaring (or changing) the name is a gated round like any other —
the one non-doc property edit the ceremony admits, itemized at the
gate as KB NAMED. Identity may change hands at a gate; it never
quietly vanishes.

Databases on a shared DBMS all carry the engine's in-band identity
stamp, and the stamps together are the machine's registry of names:
every load reads the target's stamp first, and a database another
knowledge base holds refuses by name before a byte is written. A
knowledge base is born with its own names (`init` writes settings
naming the canon database after the KB and the working copy
`<kb>-scratch`), so two KBs sharing a machine cannot collide by
default and cannot collide by accident.

Born with names, born connected: birth also creates the KB's own
databases and users on the machine — a query-only reader for answering (a canon
claim carries its query receipt, so the live read path is
load-bearing) and a writer for the working copy — idempotently,
through the same admin connection that creates databases, with
generated credentials in the KB's own settings and never in
source control. The project scaffold offers both connections to
any session opened in the repo, automatically-with-option: the
client asks before enabling them. A machine that cannot manage
users refuses plainly, naming what to do by hand; the
`connections` verb re-runs the birth step any time, changing
nothing that already stands.

One rule keeps the registry honest across renames: the stamp follows
its own line's adopted name, judged by identity, never by trust. A
database whose stamp names the FORMER holder is accepted when its
recorded base identity is one this line has ever held — the round that
adopts a knowledge base's name must land on databases stamped before
the name moved — and the acceptance is read aloud ("followed the
knowledge base to its adopted name"), never silent. Another knowledge
base's database still refuses by name, unchanged.

## Pocket Universes: a private line of one knowledge base

A branch is an independent line of truth within one KB. A **Pocket
Universe** is a branch cut as a clone of canon and declared so: `branch` cuts it
and the engine writes the declaration itself — who cut it, who is
invited, the canon identity and sequence it forked from — carried
in-band in two places (a [Pocket Universe] row on the line, and the
universe database's own stamp). The declaration is a fact about the
line, set aside from its content identity, so a Pocket Universe's rounds
diff clean against canon's. `branches` lists every line and what it is,
and readability is the creator's until they invite someone —
permissions gate who may SEE a Pocket Universe; the isolation
itself is the line ([lenses.md](lenses.md)).

Inside a Pocket Universe, everything is ordinary: its own working copy, its own
gated rounds, its own chained log. Canon is physically out of reach —
an apply scoped to a Pocket Universe refuses the live canon
database by name. What
succession adopts is the line stripped of its declaration: canon is never
a Pocket Universe. Discard a Pocket Universe and nothing anywhere happened; keep
working it while canon keeps moving, and merge is how the two
meet. A spent one retires by the owner's word — every round taken
up, the record standing whole and closed, the databases dropped,
further rounds refusing by name — and the roster hides retired
lines unless asked.

## Reading the diagram

- **Three lifelines, read top to bottom.** What passes directly
  between submitter and machinery is material and notice — artifacts
  in, the reading shown back, escalations surfacing, answers out. Every
  *decision* crosses through the middle column, the gates — that is
  the point.
- **The plan gate** ratifies *the reading*: how the artifact was
  understood — its structure, what each span is (table, procedure,
  rule-prose, carried flavor), and any concepts the mapping wants to
  create. Nothing about the reading is fait accompli; the machine's
  understanding is reviewable before it becomes work.
- **The diff gate** ratifies *the change*: every fact, beside the
  sentence it came from, with the blast radius named (whose work it
  touches, who gets notified). The convergence loop delivers to this
  gate only what agents could not resolve themselves — the submitter
  never sees finding 3 of 64; they see "these need your word."
- **The machinery's stations, in a phrase each**: *fingerprint & keep*
  — recognize the artifact forever and preserve the original untouched;
  *reading room* — understand its structure and what each piece claims;
  *scratch mapping* — translate the reading into canon's own
  vocabulary (the judgment step); *proposal* — bundle the changes,
  frozen by content; *convergence loop* — regenerate cold, judge
  against the original, burn down every finding agents can fix;
  *approval freeze* — record the ruling, by name, against exactly what
  was reviewed; *apply* — replay exactly what was approved or nothing;
  *event log* — archive the change and its undo, chained so history
  cannot be quietly rewritten; *serve* — answer from canon, cited,
  scoped to the asker.
- **The Pocket** (upper lane) is deliberately gateless: anyone can make
  a copy, experiment, interrogate, and discard. Canon is untouchable
  from inside a Pocket; a proposal carries only what the submitter chose
  to keep.
- **After canon** (Serve → Live with canon), the relationship
  inverts: the submitter asks and the machinery answers — scoped to
  their clearance, cited to its sources, in the medium the evidence
  lives in (images shown, audio played, video cued to the moment). A
  new question that canon cannot answer often becomes the next
  artifact — the loop's re-entry.
