## Slice 1 (built) and what waits

Built: graph/lens.py (declarations, fold, compile, apply, explain,
require — pure logic over the in-memory graph value), the lens-scoped
export, the keeper walkthrough as an executable test, floors for the
coherence and flat-deny rules. Declarations rode a YAML surface until
the residence ceremony landed them as citizens; the file surface
retired in the YAML-cleansing arc — the graph is the only
declaration surface, read by declarations_from_graph.

Built in slice 2 (session activation): compile_lens takes the hats
worn this session — subject as one group or an iterable of groups
(each closed upward through its own containers), and `without=` to
subtract named groups after the fold. "Exit the branch" is a
lens subtraction, no membership edit; an empty active set is honest
assume-deny, never an error.

**The residence ceremony was RULED and landed** (owner: "go for it",
after the Griptape Nodes expressibility check — the
model expresses the owner's node-library permissions system with zero
kernel additions; hierarchy as overlapping memberships, posture as
class-kind choice). At the kernel ceremony: **[Visibility Group]**
and **[Visibility Class]** join as concepts — named Visibility Group,
not Group, because boundary rule 6 caught the bare name colliding with
a knowledge base's own domain concept: the kernel never claims a word
a project's domain may need. The edge vocabulary
(MEMBER_OF, IN_CLASS, ALLOWED, DENIED flat-only, INCLUDES, MANAGES) is
admitted by the ceremony's Decision row; specs land with first
consumers. The project ontology binds both labels as
implicit delta-born citizens, the Requirement pattern. The engine
grew declarations_from_graph (one lint, two surfaces), the
fold-touching self-visibility in compile_lens (the A/B/C case: you
see your hats and the doors they open; the roster hides by edge
coherence), and the uniform refusal surface (REDACTED_REFUSAL — one
shared string; candid explain is the curator surface). The residence
round (the judgment masking class as the first Visibility Class
citizen + the ruling Decision rows) rides the ordinary
delta/approve/canonize path.

The meta-rule is fully ruled (all four questions + the deferred
developer tier); belief divergence is parked on the owner's word;
MANAGES enforcement is held for multi-user.

The original proposal, kept for the record:

  Kernel (metaontology.yaml), two concepts by the Procedure precedent:

      Group:
        instance_of: Concept
        doc: A subject of visibility. Individuals are size-1 groups;
          groups nest. The fold of a subject's groups is what a lens
          compiles from.
      Visibility Class:
        instance_of: Concept
        doc: A named set of graph elements that visibility verdicts
          speak about — the only permission-bearing unit. kind is
          knowledge (assume-deny) or masking (assume-allow).

  Ground edge vocabulary (authored, never derived): MEMBER_OF
  (Group → Group, the nesting), IN_CLASS (any element → Visibility
  Class, the membership), ALLOWED / DENIED (Group → Visibility
  Class, the verdicts — denies flat-only, enforced by the lint),
  INCLUDES (Visibility Class → Visibility Class, knowledge
  grant-inheritance). Class kind and the label/type selectors ride as
  properties on the Visibility Class citizen. After the ceremony:
  lenses.yaml's content lands as citizens via an ordinary canon
  round, lens.py grows a from-graph declarations reader beside the
  YAML one, and the intake seal becomes physically enforceable.
- **Belief divergence** [deliberately open]: a lens over canon cannot
  represent a subject believing something now false (the roguelike
  map-memory / Dwarf Fortress rumor record: knowledge is a stale
  copy, not a filter). If wanted, that is per-agent overlay data — a
  different mechanism, deferred by name.
- **The meta-rule**: who may see the visibility declarations
  themselves (who-can-see-who-can-see-what) — one rule, wanted before
  multi-user.
- Physical seal enforcement for intake's sealed-reading phase rides
  this system once declarations live on the graph.

properties.body:
## The delta lifecycle (the artifact's own states)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft : agent authoring in scratch
    Draft --> MachineVerified : receipts join + lint + schema + invariants
    MachineVerified --> Draft : any check fails
    MachineVerified --> Approved : approver rules at the diff gate
    Approved --> Applied : applier replays against live (preconditions hold)
    Approved --> Draft : preconditions violated — rework against moved base
    Applied --> Superseded : a later delta revises these facts
    Applied --> Reverted : inverse applied (only while nothing built on it)
    Superseded --> [*]
    Reverted --> [*]

    note right of Approved
        Hash-pinned. Immutable.
        Any change = a new delta.
    end note
    note right of Applied
        The delta IS the event-log
        entry. Temporality for free.
    end note
```

**Implemented.** The states above are machinery now: cutting
scratch pins the base's content identity (`graph/proposals/current/
base.json`, working state, outside
the record); `delta` writes the canonical
proposal document whose sha256 IS the proposal's id; `approve` records
{delta_hash, base_hash, by} — run by the submitter or an agent on their
behalf, the record naming the human (escalation routing for protected
change classes is an open Question); and `canonize --apply` refuses
without an approval, refuses if the base moved (warn at draft, refuse
at apply — re-cut and re-review), and refuses if scratch drifted from
the approved changeset, naming the divergence item by item. On success
the round's artifacts archive to `graph/proposals/<id12>/` —
the durable audit trail: chained, inverse-carrying plain files, kept
under the knowledge base's own custody.

**Visibility and pocket readability** are designed at
[lenses.md](lenses.md): scratch rounds are the branch pattern
(branch = pinned base + delta is the contract; the clone is a cache),
permissions own only branch readability, and everything about what is
visible WITHIN a graph belongs to the lens layer, enforced on the
in-memory graph value — never to Neo4j privileges.

**Same-round endpoints — the stitch.** A round that births a
citizen in its schema edit cannot author ground edges pointing at it in
scratch (scratch is cut pre-schema, so the endpoint does not exist to
point at). Those edges ride the round's stitch file
(`graph/proposals/current/stitch.json`); the proposal document embeds
them, so the approval hash covers them and one diff gate rules the
whole round. `delta` lints the stitch narrowly (ground facts only; an
edge both of whose ends already exist belongs in scratch) and previews
its landing against the graph the round will actually produce; at
apply the stitch lands in memory after re-derivation births the
endpoints and before anything is written — the same
verify-all-before-apply-any window as every other precondition. The
inverse removes stitched edges like any other addition.

**Branches — independent lines of truth within a KB.** The default line
is live canon (the unnamed line every command works on absent a branch),
with `scratch` as its authoring copy. A *branch* is a second line WITHIN
the same knowledge base: `restore --branch <name> --base schema-only`
projects canon's schema stratum alone (`schema_only` — the complement of
`strip_derived`: the Archetype citizens and their DECLARED_IN / SUBTYPE_OF
/ Archetype-level ladder edges, no ground, no machine layers) into the
branch's own database and writes the branch's first backup, pinning the
round against that content identity — "the whole chapter, from nothing."
Each branch owns a home — `graph/branches/<name>/{export,proposals,
applied.log}` — with its own backup, chained event log, and authoring copy
(`<name>-scratch`), and `delta` / `approve` / `canonize --apply` each learn
`--branch <name>`: the full verify-all-before-apply-any round, targeting the
branch's own database and re-exporting the branch's backup and log. The
hard guard: a branch-scoped apply can never touch the live canon database —
the applier refuses by name (before any read or write) if the resolved
target is the KB's canon. The schema freeze still applies inside branches
(the lint is shared). One check relaxes by design: the **procedure
roster census** (every registered program file has its citizen) is a
completeness property of a *finished* line, and a branch mid-rebuild is
incomplete on purpose — so branch-scoped rounds carry roster findings as
advisories (in the delta report and at apply) instead of refusals, while
the default line keeps them as hard errors. The check returns to full
strength when a branch stands for succession: a branch must be
roster-clean to be adopted. Succession — a branch *becoming* canon — is
the owner's ceremony, never a flag. A branch is one line within one KB, the
atom; a *pocket* is a branch cut as a clone of canon and declared
so, its work returning through merge as the target's ordinary gated
round; a *world* (a KB that mounts other KBs through declared
dependencies) is the composition layer above, and the cross-KB
pocket bundle at one collated gate is its designed next rung.

**Succession — the ceremony itself.** `succession --branch <name>` is
the one sanctioned crossing of the branch/canon boundary. The dry run
walks every verify gate and writes nothing; the apply run walks the
same gates, then adopts. The verify phase collates, verify-all-before-apply-any: live
canon must still byte-match its own committed backup (nothing moved
outside the delta path), the branch database must byte-match the
branch's backup, both chained event logs must verify unbroken, the
branch must re-derive clean with the roster census at full strength
(the advisory era ends at this gate), the ground-facts lint must be
clean over the branch's whole line (its ground diffed from its own
schema stratum, so the round lint judges the entire line at once), and
the version anchor must ride the branch. On any failure the refusals
collate and nothing is written. Adoption proceeds capture-first: the
outgoing canon is archived as a branch (`--archive-as`, default
`superseded-<sequence>` — export, event log, and archived rounds copied
into a new branch home) BEFORE anything is overwritten; the branch's
graph is stamped with canon's next event-log sequence, so the version a
fresh connection reads keeps climbing through the ceremony; the live
canon database is rebuilt from it and the backup re-exported FROM the
database; and canon's chained log gains ONE adoption entry whose
payload slot carries the adoption record's content hash. The record —
archived with canon's rounds and doubled as the `adopted.json` marker
in the branch home — names who ruled, when, the adopted branch, its
chain tip and export identity, the canon identities before and after,
and the archive branch. Canon's chain therefore continues unbroken
across the ceremony while the branch's own fine-grained log survives in
its archived home: lineage is cryptographic, not conventional (owner
rulings, 2026-08-20). An adopted branch is provenance, not a working
line — further rounds on it refuse by name. Walk-back is a second
ceremony: rehydrate the archive branch's database (`restore --from
graph/branches/<archived>/export --database <archived>`), then run
succession on it.

**Findings are rows**: the parity harness files every judged
difference as a structured row — archived as `findings.jsonl` beside
the artifact's reading, and landed in the workspace room as
`(:Finding)-[:JUDGED_FROM]->(:Section)` with a status lifecycle (open →
escalated → ruled). Identity is content-derived, so a re-judge MERGEs
onto the same rows: worked statuses survive re-runs, findings that no
longer red are swept. The prose scorecard is a rendering of the rows.

**Verdicts are records** (the delta gate's half of the same doctrine):
every lint refusal, ceremony item, and advisory is born as a typed
record — a stable code, the subject citizen or connection as a
`{label, name}` ref, the human sentence, the standalone remedy, and the
structured particulars — and the report surfaces are renderers over the
model (`graph/report.py`). The markdown the approver reads and
`graph/reports/delta-report.json` are the SAME facts rendered twice, so
a downstream voice can re-say a verdict from its code, subject, and
remedy without parsing prose. The JSON report is a rendering, not a
frozen artifact: verdicts derive deterministically from the pinned
changeset and base, which is where tamper-evidence already lives. The
string surfaces (`lint`, `ceremony_classify`, `render_report`) remain
as renderings of the records, byte-for-byte what they always said —
golden parity tests hold them to it.

**The event log is real.** Every applied round now writes: its
**inverse** (computed mechanically from the before-images — the undo
record made executable), a **chained entry** in
`graph/proposals/applied.log` (each line naming its predecessor's hash;
rewriting any entry breaks every later link), and passes a **replay
check** at apply time — the logged delta applied to the pinned base
must reproduce the ground truth the file edits produced, every time.
File-era honesty: removals are manual approver acts canonize never
executes, so the log marks them pending; the replay compares the
executed subset. The walk-back (apply, then apply the inverse, return
byte-identical to base) is a standing test — "event log with
inverses and a demonstrated walk-back", delivered. Post-flip
the graph-native applier (the same pure applier, spoken in Cypher)
executes everything and becomes primary.

---

**Custody is the customer's.** The engine's record is plain files —
the committed backup, the round archives with their inverses, and the
hash-chained event log, each entry chained to the last so tampering
or loss shows. The engine never invokes revision control to operate:
keep the record in git, another revision control, object storage, or
plain backups, as suits the knowledge base. Where a git checkout
exists, stamps and pins note its ref as a courtesy — provenance only,
'unknown' otherwise, never load-bearing. (The owner's word, verbatim:
"Customers may not be using git to revision control their graph.")

## The diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor S as The Submitter participant G as The Two Gates participant M as The Machinery S->>M: drop artifacts — one or many
(docs, tables, images, audio, video) Note over M: fingerprint & keep each original untouched
reading room: structure, spans, content classes M->>S: "here's what I understood —
and how sure I am of each piece" loop until the reading is right S->>M: corrections, in your words M->>S: the reading, revised end S->>G: PLAN GATE — "read it that way" G->>M: the ratified reading Note over M: scratch mapping → proposal, frozen by content opt play first, commit later S->>S: Pocket copy — experiment, interrogate,
discard without trace end loop convergence — until nothing lacks a ruling Note over M: regenerate cold, judge against the originals,
burn down every finding agents can fix M->>S: escalations only — "these need your word" S->>G: rulings, recorded by name G->>M: approved omissions, carried text,
resolved contradictions end S->>G: DIFF GATE — "approve exactly this change?" G->>M: the approval, recorded by name Note over M: apply exactly what was approved, or nothing
event log: change + undo, chained history M->>S: answers — cited, scoped to your clearance,
in the medium the evidence lives in S->>M: the next artifacts — the loop begins again ```

properties.body:
## The gate's guarantees: silence never reads as held

The round machinery's rulers share one law: a check that cannot judge
refuses aloud, and an absence is a verdict, never a shrug. The named
guarantees:

- **Sweeps refuse on kernel skew.** A verdict-bearing sweep over a
  backup written by a different kernel refuses by name rather than
  judging with the wrong dictionary — a clean report over skewed
  vocabulary would be a lie of silence.
- **An undeclared kind is an ERROR, not nothing.** A citizen whose
  label has no schema row is named at derivation and refused at the
  gate; facts never ride into canon under a label the schema cannot
  see.
- **A citation that stops resolving is an ERROR, not a dropped
  edge.** A derived connection that can no longer find its target is
  named by citation and subject — a connection leaving canon silently
  is the one thing the diff gate exists to prevent. Citations resolve
  among artifact kinds first ([artifact-model.md](artifact-model.md)).
- **The landing preview judges the graph the round will actually
  produce.** The gate re-derives over base-plus-changeset, declared
  moves applied, and promotes derivation's ERRORs to refusals — what
  apply would refuse, the gate refuses first — while connections that
  would leave are itemized as advisories the approver reads. (One
  check stays advisory by design: a branch line's roster completeness,
  mid-rebuild, per the branches passage below.)

## The grade is two facets

How much of the artifact canon holds is graded twice, independently,
on the same Completeness ladder. **What the source says** — the
provenance facet (`provenance_known_at`): the documentary chain,
catalog claims, metadata. This facet DECAYS: links rot, and the
verification sweep's stale readings are its signal. **What was
examined** — the examined facet (`examined_known_at`): what eyes-on
inspection confirmed at a gate; it does not age. A maker's product
photo shows why one shared grade lied: it carries seen facts and
claimed facts at once, and a single grade either counterfeits
authority for the claims or hides the examination — museum practice
has always kept the condition report apart from the provenance.

Each facet earns its rung. **Cited**: recorded, nothing more.
**Attested** on the examined facet: a description and its confirmed
depicted contents — eyes-on is this facet's whole nature; on the
provenance facet: a location the engine has verified — a checked
chain, never merely a recorded one. **Transcribed** — the content
itself at region grain — is designed and parked on both. A legacy
single grade reads by what it always meant — Cited as the source-says
facet, Attested as the examined facet — and a round touching a
legacy-graded artifact is told to split it while it's there.

## The isolation decision

**RULED for the buildout:** the scratch-copy column
carries the agentic era's first implementation — in the derived era,
"copy base to scratch" is `python -m graph load --database scratch`
(rebuild from sources), agent writes land on top through the scoped
`neo4j-scratch` connection, and canonization applies the approved delta
graph-natively to canon (THE FLIP, below), editing no source files.
**The pocket-universe question was settled
by shipping the scratch-copy column's descendant**: a pocket is a
branch cut as a clone of canon, its work merged back through the
ordinary gate. The table below stays as the record of the briefing
that framed it.

Where does the scratch live? Three candidate mechanics, no decision baked
in. The owner's standing observation frames the stakes: **cracking
pocket-universe-on-live makes the temporality problem largely disappear**
— work never touches canon until approved, so back-out is mostly about
*unapplied* work, which is free.

| | Overlay-on-live | Scratch copy | Lock the graph |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanics | draft assertions live in the same store, tagged (grade/named-graph-style); queries resolve overlay-first, fall back to canon | clone the DB (or rebuild base into a second database); work there | single writer; agent works directly on live behind a lock; approval = unlock, rejection = rollback |
| Isolation | weak-by-default — every canonical query must scope correctly, forever | strong — leakage impossible | none during work; the lock *is* the boundary |
| Cross-references to canon | trivial (same store) | need the copy to be complete | trivial |
| Diff ergonomics | the overlay IS the diff | external comparison (kernel's extract-delta does the work) | transaction log is the diff |
| Cost | query-scoping machinery + tombstones ("canon has X; pocket removes X") | copy time/space per proposal | forecloses concurrent sessions and long-running review; a week-long open proposal blocks everything |
| Prior art | RDF named graphs; Datomic speculative `with`; assertion grades (the source-authority ladder as the pocket boundary — "querying at a trust threshold") | CAD workspaces; today's branch-and-rebuild | classic single-writer DB |
| Temporality bonus | subsumes it (the owner's observation): tentative work is *visible but graded*, never canon until promoted | subsumes it: tentative work is elsewhere entirely | does NOT subsume it — mutations hit live during work; needs the event log to be trustworthy from day one |

Note the grade-based overlay quietly unifies three prior designs: the
confidence buckets from the ingest workflow, the source-authority ladder
(deferred Question), and Judgment-style supersession. "Pocket" stops
being a place and becomes an epistemic status.

## The keeper walkthrough (the design's acceptance story) [owner]

A keeper named Bramble must know where the hidden Emberstone lies —
but only while the owner works in one workspace branch. Order of
events: cut the branch (readability creator-only — the branch IS the
isolation); author the Emberstone fact and its Emberstone Lore class
membership in the branch; author the grant (Bramble × Emberstone Lore)
→ allow in the branch — the grant is itself branch content, so
"temporary permission" needs no mechanism at all; ask "what does
Bramble know?" inside the branch (the branch selects the reality,
Bramble's folded lens filters within it — she knows Universal + Keeper
knowledge + the Emberstone; other keepers do not); exit the branch
(view returns to canon, where there is nothing to know); land it via
the ordinary delta round (fact, class, grant become canon rows) or
discard the branch clean.

## The kernel stays honest

The corpus's canon embeds the kernel's schema stratum, and this repo
ships both — so a guard test holds the embedded kernel byte-equal to
the packaged metaontology: a kernel ceremony physically cannot merge
without migrating the shipped canon in the same change set. The general migration operation shipped as `python -m graph
kernel-migrate`: a consuming world runs it when it adopts a new
engine, and verdict-bearing commands refuse on the kernel skew until
it has — the guard stays as the forcing function.

## The ladder, and what waits above it

The shipped composition reads bottom-up: a **branch** is one line
within one KB, the atom; a **Pocket Universe** is a branch with a
declaration and a merge path; a **world** is a KB that declares other KBs
as its dependencies and reaches their citizens through bookmarks.

Two rungs are designed and not shipped, named here so their absence
never reads as an oversight: the **cross-KB Pocket
Universe** — one invitation-ready bundle of them, one per member KB
the work mutates, read-pins for the rest, landing at one collated gate with
verify-all-before-apply-any extended across every member KB — and
**world navigation**, the world as a context a reader steps into that
routes questions to the right member KB. Both wait on evidence from
worlds in real use; each arrives, when it arrives, through its own
gated design dialogue.

## The micro-kernel: five organs, fixed forever

| Organ | Exists today? |
|---|---|
| copy-base-to-scratch | exists — `restore --database scratch` cuts the round from canon's committed backup (post-flip). Scale path: relevant-subset copies (recon's neighborhood + boundary, fetch-on-demand), guarded by apply-time preconditions against full live |
| extract-delta | new (the committed export snapshot diff is its rebuild-era ancestor) |
| apply-delta (+ precondition checks) | **new — the genuinely novel organ**, together with the event log |
| derived post-pass | exists (metamodel, projections, term index) — needs re-rooting from "empty base" to "any base" |
| check-runner over `.cypher` invariants | exists (`make check`) — suite needs persistent-era additions |

Plus one lint: **ground-facts-only** on deltas (trivial). Nothing else.
Every future capability lands as *data* — schema, glossary, recipes,
checks, proposals — never as kernel growth.

**THE FLIP IS DECLARED** (owner ruling): the graph
is primary. The export is the backup (restore drilled), the event log
is the version control of record. **The freeze is lifted**:
canonize --apply is graph-native — pinned changeset onto the ground
layer, machine layers re-derived (one derivation codepath with the
bootstrap extractor, proven byte-identical), canon loaded, backup
re-exported from the database, event log chained. Data-plane intake is
open. **The schema inverted**: the schema stratum is ground on
the graph — Archetype citizens and their edges are authored truth,
preserved by the strip and never rebuilt by derivation; post-bootstrap
commands read the schema from the graph (`ontology_from_graph`), the
anchor's version auto-stamps from the event-log sequence, and the from-sources era has since closed — every knowledge base is born graph-native or ingested through the front door.
Schema changes ride the SCHEMA CEREMONY: an ordinary owner-gated round may add a new declared concept, birth a new label (a spec-carrying row with nothing yet underneath it), edit a schema row's doc text, add an alias to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an existing citizen — additions only), edit a label's render mapping (the table layout it renders through — add, change, or remove; the loader never reads it, so nothing moves), release a label's source registration (a program label's files leave once every citizen carries its own body and cites no file; any other label's source rows leave as archaeology no verb reads), declare a taxonomy link (an authored kind-of connection into a concept, both citizens existing), adopt the knowledge base's own declared name on its anchor (KB NAMED — identity may change hands at a gate, never quietly vanish), or remove an unreferenced schema row — itemized under the delta report's marked ceremony section, whose approval IS the ceremony ruling. A round may also declare moves — a rename of the world's own label or concept, or a re-homing of named citizens under a kind of what they were — itemized and guarded at the same gate, the approval covering them. Changes to an existing label or spec move data underneath them and stay refused: they ride the migration charter.

properties.body:
## The narrative: you hand the agent a doc with a table

Running example: `sources/03-the-hollow-wood.md` arrives, containing a
Beasts table. "Let's intake this."

### Phase 1 — Recon

**What you experience:** nothing yet. The agent reads quietly for a minute.

**Under the hood:** the agent reads the doc cold and identifies, by
**semantic comprehension**, every entity, relationship, and rule the
content asserts — regardless of casing or formatting discipline (not
everyone capitalizes their terms; identification is reasoning about
meaning, never a word search). Pronouns and other indirect references get
special attention — "they pass it to their thing" requires resolving who
*they* is and what *it* refers to — so recon may take **multiple
disambiguation passes**, and a reference that stays genuinely ambiguous
is escalated to the owner as a question rather than guessed at. Each
candidate the agent identifies is then
**resolved deterministically** through the term index (resolves / stub
exists / unknown — that half stays exact), and read-only Cypher explores
the neighborhood: existing citizens the table touches, the stub worklist
("Beast" may already be a stub from a prior round), prior Judgment rows.
The mechanical capitalized-run sweep still runs, demoted to a **backstop
tripwire** — it catches candidates comprehension missed, never defines
the candidate set. Output: a classification with confidence buckets —
*relates-to*, *introduces*, *uncertain* — and a routing call (which graph
this belongs to). The live graph is touched only by reads.

### Phase 2 — The plan gate (yours)

**What you experience:** the what's-this-about proposal — what the table
is, what it maps onto, what's new — and it leads with an **implications
preview** in plain terms: what you GET ("the Beasts become queryable — a
reader can ask 'which Beast guards the Hollow Gem?'"), what you LOSE or
change ("the Chapter's prose meaning narrows to the Beasts on this
list"), and what it AFFORDS later ("the Beast-lineage rules get their
anchor concepts"), each with a real example pulled from the corpus. Then
the questions only you can answer: what things should be called ("Beast
or Creature?"), how they relate to what exists, and how they behave ("do
Beast Grades form a ranked ladder?"). You rule, redirect, or park
items. This is today's intake interview, unchanged — with the
implications stated before the questions, so you rule in context.

**Under the hood:** nothing has written anywhere. The proposal's claims
were pre-checked against the graph's vocabulary during recon, so the
questions that reach you are the handful that genuinely need a human —
the mechanical majority never surfaces.

### Phase 3 — Authoring in the scratch graph

**What you experience:** "Working — I'll come back with a diff."

**Under the hood:** the kernel **copies base → scratch** (the one
concession to infrastructure; see Isolation below). Whole-graph copies
are fine while the graph is small; the scale path is a **relevant-subset
scratch** — recon's neighborhood defines the working set, the kernel
copies that plus its boundary, and anything the subset turns out to need
is fetched from base on demand. What the subset couldn't see is exactly
what the apply-time preconditions re-check against full live, so a
too-small working set degrades to a kickback, never to a wrong apply. The agent — holding
write credentials *for scratch only* — creates nodes and edges directly:
`MERGE (:Beast {name: 'Cinder Fox', ...})`, ground relationships to
existing citizens, each assertion carrying its **receipt as a property**
(`from_text`, source pointer, authority grade "agent-proposed"). If the
table is quirky, the agent also writes a normalized canonical
intermediate, hash-pinned to the source. It works the way agents
naturally work: create, query its own work, fix, iterate.

To be precise about what "ground facts only" bans — because it is NOT
"no edges": the agent freely creates nodes *and* edges that the source
asserts (a Beast, its GUARDS relationship to a Gem). What it may
never write are the **derived** kinds — classification edges
(INSTANCE_OF), signature projections (READS/MUTATES/CALLS), term-index
entries — because those are *computed from* the ground facts by the
kernel, and the whole point is that a computed layer cannot drift: if an
agent hand-wrote them, its copy would be wrong the moment the ground
facts changed, and nobody would notice. (This lesson was paid for twice
in the derived era.) The machine recomputes; nobody transcribes.

### Phase 4 — Mechanical verification

**What you experience:** still nothing. Failures never reach you.

**Under the hood:** the kernel runs queries against scratch: the
**receipts join** (every `from_text` verbatim in its source node's body —
the source doc was ingested as a Provenance citizen in this same delta),
term-index resolution (every referenced citizen exists or is new in this
delta), the **ground-facts-only lint** (any derived edge type = reject),
schema conformance against the embedded ontology, key/idempotency
checks. Violations kick straight back to Phase 3.

### Phase 5 — Derive + diff

**Under the hood:** the kernel runs the **derived post-pass** over scratch
(metamodel tower, projections, term index, ladders — today's machinery,
re-rooted) and the **invariant suite** (`.cypher` checks: placeholder
census, bijections, tower completeness). Then **extract-delta**: scratch
minus base = the changeset, including which *derived* edges appeared as
consequences of the ground facts.

### Phase 6 — Self-review

**Under the hood:** the agent reads the delta against its own plan.
Surprises — an unexpected projection, an invariant complaint, a
high-confidence item the machine bounced — are fixed (back to Phase 3) or
demoted to the uncertain bucket. Render-back fidelity diffs run where the
content is procedure-shaped.

### Phase 7 — The diff gate (yours)

**What you experience:** the delta, four ways — led, whenever the delta
touches the ontology or metaontology layers, by the **schema-changes
section with its blast radius**, before anything row-level —
1. the **implications narrative**: plain prose on what this change means,
   with concrete examples drawn from the existing corpus;
2. a statement-level table with **claim beside evidence** (each assertion
   next to its receipt);
3. the derived-consequences summary ("these 12 projection edges will
   appear");
4. a walkable view: open Bloom on scratch and *explore the proposal as a
   graph* — and because every delta member is tagged with the delta id,
   you can filter to **just the new and changed things**, or see them
   highlighted in context against unchanged canon.

Uncertain items are presented for ruling: resolve, "give it a go" (loop
to Phase 3), or park as Judgment citizens. Your approval pins the delta
by hash.

**Under the hood:** the approved artifact is now immutable. Any further
change is a new delta.

### Phase 8 — Canonization

**What you experience:** "Landed. Batch #N in the log."

**Under the hood:** the kernel's **applier** — no agent anywhere in this
phase — replays the approved delta against live, after checking
**preconditions**: every citizen the delta references still exists and
still matches the base snapshot's expectations. A violated precondition
(live moved since the scratch was cut) kicks back to Phase 7 with the
conflict named — detection, never cleverness. On success: the delta is
appended to the **event log** (it *is* the event; back-out = replaying
its recorded inverses, with the doctrine-consistent caveat that once
later deltas build on it, back-out becomes supersession). Derived
post-pass and invariants re-run on live — **including the delta's own
generated tests, which join the permanent suite from this moment**: the
next proposal is checked against this one's regressions forever.
Provenance stamped (batch id, approval, `approved_in`). The delta
artifact archives with the round.

### Phase 9 — Bookkeeping

**Under the hood:** worklist maintenance (stubs graduated, pending
instances realized), Judgment rows for parked items, glossary/skill
updates — all themselves delta content through the same pipeline, smaller
stakes. The backstop sweep should show fewer unknowns than before the
round: the worklist shrinks forever.

# The north-star workflow — two lanes, two touches

*One diagram: the submitter's lane on top, the machinery's lane beneath.
The north star's whole argument is that the two lanes exchange material
at the ends — the artifact flows in at the drop, answers flow back out at
the close — but exchange *decisions* at exactly two conversations: the
plan gate and the diff gate. Everything else the machinery does happens
without the submitter needing to know it exists. That both gates are
always present here is the mutating-job case of the agentic approach's
engagement signals — an ingest always disambiguates and always mutates;
the reconciliation is recorded once in [agentic-etl.md](agentic-etl.md)
(Invariant 6).*

properties.body:
## The one-paragraph design (owner-accepted)

Nodes and edges join named VISIBILITY CLASSES — the only
permission-bearing unit, since instances are too many to name;
individuals are size-1 GROUPS, groups nest, and verdicts are authored
on (group × class) pairs — additive allows by default, denies legal
only against flat class sets, posture fixed per lens KIND (knowledge
lenses assume-deny, masking lenses assume-allow) rather than
switchable; a LENS is the fold-down of a subject's groups compiled
into a derived resource set — machine layer, never authored — and is
enforced as a filter at the element-access layer of the in-memory
graph value (traversal never yields a masked element, so edges,
paths, aggregates, and re-derivation stay coherent by construction),
with an EXPLAIN operation that re-evaluates unfolded to name the
blocking group, consumers declaring the lenses they REQUIRE or AFFORD
so misconfiguration refuses at build time, super-admin defined as NO
LENS APPLIED, and lens-scoped EXPORTS as the one place lenses
materialize (the shipped runtime graph); Pocket Universes stay out of
the permission model entirely — they are branches on the existing
scratch/delta/canonize machinery, with permissions owning only branch
READABILITY (creator-only by default), and canonize re-tags class
membership as work becomes canon.

## The process state machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Recon : source arrives
    Recon --> PlanGate : classification + questions
    PlanGate --> Recon : approver redirects
    PlanGate --> Authoring : approver approves plan
    Authoring --> MechanicalVerify : agent done in scratch
    MechanicalVerify --> Authoring : lint/receipt/schema failure (kickback)
    MechanicalVerify --> DeriveAndDiff : all checks pass
    DeriveAndDiff --> SelfReview : delta extracted
    SelfReview --> Authoring : surprise found (kickback)
    SelfReview --> DiffGate : delta matches plan
    DiffGate --> Authoring : approver course-corrects / "give it a go"
    DiffGate --> Parked : items become Judgment citizens
    Parked --> DiffGate
    DiffGate --> Canonize : approver approves (delta hash-pinned)
    Canonize --> DiffGate : PRECONDITION violated (base drift, conflict named)
    Canonize --> Bookkeeping : applied + event logged + derived pass + invariants
    Bookkeeping --> [*]

    note right of Authoring
        Agent writes SCRATCH only.
        Ground facts only.
        Receipts as properties.
    end note
    note right of Canonize
        Kernel only — no agent
        holds a pen in this state.
    end note
```

## The reading room (comprehension graph)

*Designer ruling (recorded as the canon-is-the-knowledge Decision row).*

**Canon is the knowledge.** The canonical graph holds Concepts and
Judgments, plus thin provenance anchors. A dumped artifact's *insides* —
its section tree, bodies, order, heading hierarchy, embedded-table
references — are the machine's understanding of the artifact, and they
live in the **comprehension graph**: a separate workspace the pipeline
builds per intake round (`python -m graph comprehend <artifact>`).

The lifecycle is **build → archive → dispose**:

- **Build** — one well-known workspace database (`comprehension`), wiped
  per round like scratch. Never a standing database per asset.
- **Archive** — at round close the room serializes to small flat files
  under `graph/comprehension/<name>-<fingerprint12>/` (kept with the
  record, like `graph/export/`). Any set of archives batch-imports back into the room
  (`--recall`) for browsing; rounds coexist because every citizen
  carries its artifact's fingerprint.
- **Dispose** — the live room is wiped (`--dispose`); the archives are
  the record.

**Canon's side of the line** (the thinning): canon keeps one thin
anchor per artifact — the citizen, carrying a content-hash
`fingerprint` — and citations are **artifact + span**: a procedure's
`specified_in` names `{artifact, section, approved_hash}` and is
verified against the file's bytes directly; the SPECIFIED_IN edge lands
on the Artifact with the section as edge detail. No section citizens,
no mentions index on canon (the room's assertions layer is the
successor; until it lands, "which sections discuss X" is answered by
text search).

This thinning is the rule for a canon that is ABOUT a domain — where
a dropped artifact is *evidence for* the knowledge, not the knowledge
itself. A corpus whose prose IS the knowledge — its records carried as
citizens, sections with verbatim bodies on the graph — inverts the
rule by design: there the sections are canon, and once the prose lives
on the graph there is no separate source left to anchor to
([engine-as-corpus.md](engine-as-corpus.md)).

**Identity rules.** An artifact's identity is the sha256 of its bytes —
one collaborator's `Downloads` copy and another's `Temp` copy are the
same artifact; paths and titles are display metadata. Sections carry
machine-internal ids derived from fingerprint + structural position
("3f2a9c1d4e5b:2.0.1") — deterministic, so a deleted archive's structure
recomputes bit-identical from the immutable bytes. Quirks inside a
dumped artifact (duplicate headings, skipped levels) are the pipeline's
job to absorb silently — never a submitter-facing warning. Canon-side
references (procedure citations, receipts) use fingerprint + span, never
comprehension ids, so canon integrity survives total archive loss.

**Content classes.** Every span of every section is classified so
the round-trip harness can dispatch it to the right renderer and judging
bar: `table` ({{csv:}} embeds), `procedure` (sections cited by a
procedure's specified_in), `rule-prose` (the default — the machine never
guesses flavor), and `verbatim-carried` (flavor text, approver-assigned
at the plan gate, never deduced). The **carried fraction** — how much
prose is carried verbatim — is the honesty valve's metric, reported per
artifact so "just store it verbatim" cannot silently become the whole
round-trip proof; the ceiling is approver-set and enforced by the
harness.

**The parity harness** consumes the classes: `python -m graph
roundtrip --scope <artifact> --draft <regeneration>` judges a draft at
the functional-parity bar — chapter scope, never section-by-section
(structure is free): tables at cell-level content equivalence with row
integrity, procedures against the approved programs' atoms (answer keys
add behavior teeth), prose through the claim-diff judge,
approved flavor byte-intact, inventions checked once against the
combined original corpus. One scorecard, every red named, exit nonzero —
no human in the comparison step. The cold draft itself is produced by
the fenced regeneration loop; the harness only judges.

The plan gate reads its structure view from the room; the assertions and
canon-impact layers of comprehension join with the first intake round
that runs through it.

properties.body:
## The render contract and the flip

`docs` output is **deterministic within a version** — same canon, same
bytes, held by a golden render snapshot — and the stub contract
narrows to: names resolve, descriptions match, output complete. It was
never byte-frozen across versions; records evolve through rounds like
any canon. **Byte-parity with the prose files was the flip criterion, never a
permanent contract**: each record's canon had to reassemble to the
exact bytes of its file, and when every record passed, the flip was
taken — `docs` serves canon, and the files, their packaged mirrors,
and the parity tests are retired. The canon is the source of truth
now; nothing downstream noticed, which was the point.

## The words this document uses

Plain-language definitions up front, so the narrative reads without
insider knowledge:

- **Ground fact** — something the source material directly asserts ("the
  Cinder Fox guards the Hollow Gem"). Contrast **derived fact** —
  something the machine can compute from ground facts (classification
  towers, "which procedures read a Beast's Grade"). People and agents
  write ground facts; machines recompute derived facts from scratch every
  time, so nobody's hand-written copy can silently rot.
- **Scratch graph** — a private working copy of the database. Nothing
  done there touches the real one.
- **The reading room (comprehension graph)** — where the machine's
  understanding of a dumped artifact lives: its fingerprint identity and
  its section tree (bodies, order, nesting, embedded-table refs). Canon
  is the knowledge; the artifact's insides are comprehension material (see
  "The reading room" below).
- **Delta** — the complete, itemized list of proposed changes (see
  "Anatomy of a delta"). It is the thing you review, the thing you
  approve, and the permanent record of what changed.
- **Receipt** — a verbatim quote from the source attached to a proposed
  fact, so every claim can be checked against evidence.
- **Stub** — a concept the graph knows *exists* but hasn't modeled yet;
  the running to-do list of ideas awaiting real treatment.
- **Judgment citizens** — open questions, decisions, and to-dos stored in
  the graph itself, with history, instead of in loose notes.
- **The two gates** — the two moments that require you: approving the
  *plan* (before any work) and approving the *diff* (before anything
  becomes real).

# The worlds layer — many knowledge bases, one engine

One engine serves many knowledge bases. A game's rules can be one KB; a
creature almanac someone else publishes can be another that the first
merely uses; a world is the context that gathers them and knows how
they relate. This record tells the layer whole as it shipped: how
knowledge bases share one machine without colliding, how one KB
reaches into another on purpose, how a single KB carries private lines
of itself, and how lines reconcile. The composition above this — a
Pocket Universe spanning a whole world, the world as a navigable context — is
designed and named at the end, not shipped.

Everything here obeys the standing rules of the round machinery
([agentic-etl.md](agentic-etl.md)): every crossing is declared, every
verdict is a record, and silence never reads as held — a ruler that
finds nothing wrong says so.

properties.body: ## Trust

# Two Ontology Layers

<!-- Engine-owned doctrine. Travels with the engine (like metaontology.yaml).
     Consuming knowledge bases import this into their agent instructions so it is
     standing context for ALL work, not an on-demand procedure. -->

The graph schema has two layers with different ownership and change ceremony:

- **Engine metaontology** (`graph/metaontology.yaml`): the project-agnostic
  kernel — the `Archetype` label, `INSTANCE_OF`, the four roots (**Concept**,
  **Facet**, **Provenance**, **Judgment**), and the common facet library
  (Ordered, Exclusive, Stateful, ...). The membership test: *would a kid's
  storybook project need it?* Changes here are cross-project design decisions
  of the highest weight — never made casually, never as a silent side effect
  of intake, always via explicit design dialogue with the owner. That
  dialogue may happen at a round's gate: a kernel ceremony may be declared
  and ruled mid-round when the round's evidence demands it, including a
  conditionally pre-authorized enabling engine change ("only on a real
  refusal, with its own tests"). What makes it a ceremony is the explicit
  owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, and the semver bump + ledger line
  riding the same change set — the dialogue and the record, not the
  calendar.
  A canon's committed backup embeds the kernel stratum it was
  built with, so the ceremony's change set also migrates every
  canon the engine repo ships (`python -m graph kernel-migrate`)
  — and a consuming knowledge base runs the same migration when
  it adopts the new engine: mutating commands refuse on the skew
  until it does.
  The splice keeps the world's own knowledge: the kernel wins every
  key it defines, and any enrichment a canon has laid on a kernel
  citizen beyond that rides the migration unchanged — named in the
  report, never silently dropped.

- **Project ontology** (the graph's own schema stratum): everything
  THIS knowledge base derived — its domain concepts, labels, catalogs,
  relationships, project-specific facets. Since the schema inversion the
  schema lives ON THE GRAPH as ground citizens — the Archetype
  stratum, read by `ontology_from_graph` — and this is the owner's
  daily surface, following the ontology-has-one-owner rules.
  The from-sources era is closed: every knowledge base is born graph-native or ingested through the front door, and an early corpus's bootstrap files are archaeology
  in the project's own history, never a provenance surface. It versions from the
  event-log sequence, auto-stamped on the graph's Ontology anchor at
  apply, with an optional free-text `tag` beside it — semver stays with the kernel, whose bumps are ceremony (owner ruling).
  Three spec fields keep their stories here: `values:` on an ordered
  concept is the ladder's declared order, read when the schema
  stratum is seeded or migrated; `reader:` is a label's lift
  declaration — how its citizens' bodies and sections are read —
  guarded at derivation, which refuses an unknown kind by name; and
  a citizen born by reference under a declared `implicit:` label is
  itemized at the gate, never silent.
  Schema changes ride the SCHEMA CEREMONY: an ordinary owner-gated round may add a new declared concept, birth a new label (a spec-carrying row with nothing yet underneath it), edit a schema row's doc text, add an alias to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an existing citizen — additions only), edit a label's render mapping (the table layout it renders through — add, change, or remove; the loader never reads it, so nothing moves), release a label's source registration (a program label's files leave once every citizen carries its own body and cites no file; any other label's source rows leave as archaeology no verb reads), declare a taxonomy link (an authored kind-of connection into a concept, both citizens existing), adopt the knowledge base's own declared name on its anchor (KB NAMED — identity may change hands at a gate, never quietly vanish), or remove an unreferenced schema row — itemized under the delta report's marked ceremony section, whose approval IS the ceremony ruling. A round may also declare moves — a rename of the world's own label or concept, or a re-homing of named citizens under a kind of what they were — itemized and guarded at the same gate, the approval covering them. Changes to an existing label or spec move data underneath them and stay refused: they ride the migration charter.

label: [Section]
name: Verification is the location row's own fact

properties.body:
## Verification is the location row's own fact

What the engine actually read is stamped where the reading happened:
on the location row. At apply, every file location of every artifact
the round touched is read and stamped — `verified_fingerprint`,
`verified_at_sequence`, `size` — and a file location that cannot be
read refuses the round, collated, before anything is written. The
receipts sweep reads the same rows later, so "is the file still what
canon verified?" is a query, never a memory.

A non-text artifact (an image, a PDF, audio) enters at its **floor
receipt**: `python -m graph receipt <file>` prints the fingerprint,
size, and the medium the bytes declare, and the comprehension room
refuses to read it for structure plainly, receipt in hand — what the
engine cannot comprehend it still identifies, and silence never reads
as held.

Artifact-hood follows the taxonomy: a citizen whose kind descends from
[Artifact] is an artifact to every rule here — the gate, the stamp,
and the sweep all fold the kinds. Citations resolve among artifact
kinds first, and a citation the machinery can no longer resolve is an
ERROR by name, never a silently dropped connection.

properties.body: ## Voice

## What each lane never sees

The submitter never sees: fingerprints, content hashes, deltas,
inverses, chain verification, content classes, scratch databases. Those
words appear in the lower lane only.

The machinery never decides: what counts as flavor, whether an omission
is acceptable, how a contradiction resolves, when an experiment becomes
a proposal, what a Theme means. Those are ruling verbs, and every one
is recorded with the ruler's name.

properties.body:
## What the citizens are

- **Conduct records** (the skills' full procedures) become kernel
  **[Procedure]** citizens, Completeness ruled per record at its intake
  gate — expected mostly Attested: an asserted signature over a prose
  body that lives on the graph as that record's own section citizens,
  `SPECIFIED_IN` pointing at citizens, not files. A procedure defined
  in an interactive session is legitimate provenance; nothing demands
  a file path.
- **Design records** become section-level citizens — the record an
  ordered container, each section carrying its verbatim body — with
  claim-level promotion only where the source is already enumerated
  (numbered rules, tenet lists, glossaries). Cross-references that
  name sections and invariants become edges.

This is the scoped side of the reading-room thinning
([agentic-etl.md](agentic-etl.md)): here the prose IS the knowledge,
so sections are citizens by design — once the prose lives on the
graph, there is no separate source left to anchor to.

**Machinery marking extends to the project layer.** The customer of
the whole system is the world's designer, and to them this corpus is
entirely under the hood — agents are staff, not customers. Its labels
therefore wear the machinery brackets (the kernel's marking
convention, applied by owner ruling at the layer's first gate); ground
citizens keep their natural names, and the standing
`NOT STARTS WITH '['` filter keeps every such catalog off
customer-facing surfaces by construction.

label: [Section]
name: What worlds do with the conduct

properties.body:
## What worlds do with the conduct

The engine ships the trunk: tenets, procedures, doctrine — versioned
by the pin. Each world is expected to **tailor the conduct to its own
experience**: the door's voice is learned live from that world's canon
([front-door-tenets.md](front-door-tenets.md)), and a world keeps its
own local skills alongside the engine's. Two worlds at different pins
run different conduct on purpose — skew is a chosen consequence of
pinning, and the pin is the sync mechanism.

## Why each piece (the dialogue, condensed)

- **Classes, not instances** [record]: the owner's Approach A
  (subject-side ACLs) and Approach B (resource-side sets) are duals;
  every surveyed system authors subject-side and ANSWERS list-shaped
  questions resource-side, compiled (Zanzibar's Leopard index, OPA
  partial evaluation, the owner's own Griptape fold-down). A authors;
  B serves; B is derived, never authored — the project's existing
  authored-vs-machine doctrine applied to permissions.
- **Deny discipline** [record]: deny × nested groups is where the
  record draws hard lines (OpenFGA refuses recursive-membership ×
  exclusion at model-build time; AuthZed: "start with no access and
  build up"). Denies here are leaf verdicts against FLAT classes only.
  The owner's tri-state No-Opinion survives — it is what makes
  "the deny didn't match" and "nothing said anything" distinguishable
  (Neo4j's documented fail-open deny is the cautionary tale).
- **Posture per lens kind, never a global switch** [record + owner]:
  no security system surveyed ships switchable assume-allow (XACML's
  configurable algebra is its least-loved feature; the field drifted
  to Cedar's fixed default-deny) — but the game-design record runs the other
  way (fog of war, roguelike map memory are assume-allow with
  carve-outs). Both are right in their kind: knowledge lenses
  assume-deny; masking lenses assume-allow.
- **Enforcement at the element-access layer** [record]: front-door
  result stripping leaks whatever was computed over hidden data
  (counts, path existence — the Postgres RLS side-channel record);
  query rewriting suits SQL, not arbitrary traversal. Datomic's
  d/filter is the fit: filter the in-memory database VALUE so
  traversal never yields a masked element. Our read path is already
  an immutable GraphData; strip_derived is the ur-lens. Coherence
  rules the approaches missed: an edge is visible only if both
  endpoints are; derived layers RE-DERIVE under the lens, never
  filter through it.
- **Explain from day one** [owner's Griptape lesson + record]: the
  fold loses which-group-blocked; decide on the fold, re-evaluate
  unfolded to explain. Cedar's fixed algebra exists for exactly this
  comprehension property.
- **Super admin = no lens** [record, unanimous]: an enforcement-layer
  bypass (BYPASSRLS, Cedar's implicit default), never a subject
  granted everything — under any-deny-wins a modeled admin loses to
  the first deny, and every new class would have to remember them.
- **Pocket Universes are branches, not permissions** [record + owner]:
  every system whose job is isolated adds-AND-removals with later
  merge is a branch system (TerminusDB does it for a knowledge graph;
  tombstones appear in the record only as internal versioning
  implementation, never as the user-facing permission model — masking
  a removal is intrinsically a deny and imports every deny warning
  into steady state). The scratch round with base pinning and
  delta/canonize IS the branch pattern. Permissions own one small
  thing: who may see that a branch exists and read it (the lakeFS
  stance over Dolt's open reads; creator-only by default). Invitation
  is one authored verdict: (their group × the branch) → allow, read
  or write grade; an invited COLLABORATOR gets no lens, an invited
  PLAYER gets a subject's knowledge lens — branch selects the
  reality, the lens filters within it.
- **The storage contract** [owner concern, ruled]: branch = pinned
  base + delta IS the contract (base.json/delta.json already are it);
  clone, filesystem copy-on-write, and delta-overlay-over-a-shared-
  base are interchangeable implementations. Today's full clone is a
  cache, kept while cheap; the overlay (branches sharing one loaded
  immutable base value, O(delta) each) is the path when canon grows.
- **Neo4j's own RBAC: whole-database gates only** [owner + record]:
  a query-only reader on live canon; per-branch database access for pockets.
  Never label/property/traversal privileges, never DENY rules — the
  record documents static per-DB-user roles, deny-wins composition
  that cannot stack into views, fail-open property denies, and
  planner-invisible performance cliffs. The boundary sentence: Neo4j
  enforces which databases a connection may read or write; the engine
  enforces everything about what is visible within one.
- **Exports are the one materialization** [record]: the shipped
  runtime graph is a lens-scoped export (Unreal's cook: strip
  design-time data at build time, flags on the data). Live lenses
  compute fresh from canon — cached lens views reintroduce stale
  revocation (the New Enemy problem in miniature). The canonical
  backup at graph/export/ is ALWAYS lens-free.

label: [Tenet]
name: A reference number on every item

properties.body:
**T10 — A reference number on every item.** Each presented item
carries a quiet plain-English reference number — `⟨grit ·
missing-reason⟩`, shorthand "ref" — that traces one-for-one to the
raw machine record behind it. The full technical report always exists
and is always reachable; it is never what gets presented first.
(Owner-named 2026-08-26: "reference number," because customers will
likely file these into ticketing systems — and "receipt" already
means a quoted evidence sentence in the intake machinery.)

label: [Tenet]
name: Absence is information, plus an offer

properties.body:
**T14 — Absence is information, plus an offer.** When canon holds
nothing — "nothing connects Grit to Cunning" — the door says so
plainly, then offers: "Want me to note it as an open question?" Gaps
become recorded design work or are dismissed, never dead ends.

label: [Tenet]
name: Any artifact; its content and meaning

properties.body:
**T3 — Any artifact; its content and meaning.** What the designer
hands over can be anything — text, images, 3D models, songs, web
pages, annotations. The door works from what the artifact *contains
and means*, and everything downstream takes the artifact's native
form: evidence is a quoted sentence, a shown image region, a
timestamped passage, the page behind a link — whatever lets the
designer see exactly what the door saw. No text-only assumptions
anywhere in the door's conduct.

**T2 — Canon's names for canon's acts.** The system's own moments
have exactly one designer-facing vocabulary: work *enters canon*;
until then it is *pending your approval* (or sign-off). No "book."
No database, graph, delta, scratch, round, lint, or any other
machinery word — ever, on any surface. ("Canon" is deliberately
shared with the machinery's own records — one word both sides mean
the same way.)

**T11 — Every answer cites.** Answers to the designer's questions
carry where-it-lives inline, in the source's native form: a section
for text ("per Combat §4.2"), a timestamp for audio, a region for an
image, the link for a page. An uncited answer is not an answer.

**T4 — Every effect names its world.** One artifact may carry meaning
for several worlds. The door states up front which worlds an artifact
touches, groups every pending item under its world, and lets nothing
enter any canon that wasn't named. Scope is never assumed silently —
when the artifact's reach is ambiguous, naming its worlds is itself a
pending item. Sign-off is per world: approving one world's items
commits nothing anywhere else. With a single world in play, its name
rides the header once and is not belabored.

**T12 — Inferences confirm by pattern.** What the door read plainly
from the artifact enters with receipts. What it *interpreted* is
confirmed by family, not one-by-one: "I read all six 'draws on'
phrasings as the same relationship — confirm the pattern once." Each
family names its instances so any single one can be inspected or
excepted.

**T13 — Only blockers interrupt.** Judgment calls batch to the end of
the work and are cleared in one sitting. The door interrupts mid-work
only for a true blocker — a call that would distort how everything
after it is read. (The standing collate-don't-stop doctrine, extended
from errors to judgment.)

**T7 — Only what needs you.** Pending items lead. Everything that
checked clean compresses to a single line, expandable on request. The
door never walks the full account unasked.

**T8 — Severity draws the frame** *(provisional)*. When the designer
could supply the missing piece on the spot, the door *requests* it
("Provide the reason, or drop it") — the stop is implied. When no
inline answer could make the thing legal — an attempt to rewrite
canon's own structure, or to hand-edit records the machine maintains
— the door states the *verdict* plainly, then what would clear it.
Owner: "start with that as the line, try it to see the feel" —
revisit on evidence from live gates.

label: [Tenet]
name: The designer's language, learned live from canon

properties.body:
**T1 — The designer's language, learned live from canon.** Every
domain noun the door speaks is discovered by querying canon at
conversation time: what a thing is, what kind it belongs to, what its
own doc text says. Nothing is hand-mapped. No cheat sheets anywhere:
not in the knowledge base, not in skills. If the door speaks a world
well, it is because that world's canon describes itself well — a gap
in the door's speech is a gap in canon, fixed by adding to canon.

**T9 — The door holds no opinions.** Asked to argue, the door takes
no side: it marshals canon's evidence *both ways* — counts,
citations, precedents, and what canon lacks — and hands the ruling
back. "Convince me" gets the strongest case in each direction, never
the door's taste. The designer rules; the door informs.

**T5 — The editor's desk.** Impersonal, itemized, decisions-first.
Numbered pending items; each ends in an arrow naming the actions that
resolve it. Counts over adjectives ("14 additions," not "many
changes"). No warmth padding, no apology, no first-person narrative
of the door's own labors.

label: [Tenet]
name: The item's anatomy: rulable from itself alone

properties.body:
**T6 — The item's anatomy: rulable from itself alone.** Every pending
item makes four moves, in order: (1) the question, up front, in the
designer's terms; (2) the current state and the proposed state, with
the evidence presented inline in the artifact's native form — the
sentence quoted, the image region shown, the passage timestamped —
beside canon's current state, never a pointer to either; (3) the
implications: what each choice actually means going forward; (4) the
ask restated as a direct action item, so however long the explanation
ran, the item ends where the hand acts. An item that requires opening
anything else before it can be ruled on is a defect.

**T15 — Threads end in a record.** A debate never evaporates. Every
thread ends with the ruling and the designer's stated reason kept on
record — the designer's words, not a paraphrase — or, unresolved,
with the question noted as open. A resolved thread leaves a trail:
when the same question resurfaces from a future artifact, it returns
with the prior thread attached, so debate resumes from the last
ruling instead of restarting cold.
